pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce paduṭṭhena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ dukkham-anveti cakkaṁ va vahato padaṁ.
english: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, (their quality is) made by mind, if with a base mind one speaks or acts, through that suffering follows him like a wheel (follows) the ox’s foot.
notes: This meaning of this line has to be understood by reference to the whole verse, which is an ethical statement about the quality of mind bringing suitable returns. I believe many mistranslations have occurred by treating it as a descriptive, quasi-Abhidhammic, statement about the relationship between mind and mental objects.

In parallel versions the reading is always given as manojavā, impelled (or driven) by mind, which might seem more congruous with the early teaching. This reading also occurs in Peṭakopadesa, PTS p. 164, which reads in the context of this verse: Manojavā ti yattha mano gacchati tattha ime dhammā gacchantī ti manojavā; impelled by mind means wherever the mind goes there these thoughts go, (therefore) impelled by mind is said.
It is curious that vahatu, an ox, is not found in PED or CPED.
We see here and it many other places that the verb is made to work twice; in Pāḷi the meaning is clear, but in English we have to restate the verb, otherwise it is ambiguous.

This verse evidently belongs with the following one, and must have been composed together, but the commentary assigns very different occasions to their composition. The same could be said about many others pairs of verses, and not only in this Chapter.

pali: Manopubbaṅgamā dhammā, manoseṭṭhā manomayā, manasā ce pasannena bhāsati vā karoti vā, tato naṁ sukham-anveti chāyā va anapāyinī.
english: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, (their quality is) made by mind, if with pure mind one speaks or acts, through that happiness follows him like a shadow which does not depart.

pali: “Akkocchi maṁ, avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ, ahāsi me”, ye ca taṁ upanayhanti veraṁ tesaṁ na sammati.
english: “He abused me, he struck at me, he overcame me, he robbed me,” those who bear ill-will towards this their hatred is never appeased.
notes: Presumably me is ablative, he took from me, he robbed from me.

We might have expected the genitive, not the nominative, form here, yesaṁ, for those..., the line could easily be rewritten to fit the metre: yesañ-ca upanayhanti, and in the next line: yesaṁ na upanayhanti.

pali: “Akkocchi maṁ, avadhi maṁ, ajini maṁ, ahāsi me”, ye taṁ na upanayhanti veraṁ tesūpasammati.
english: “He abused me, he struck at me, he overcame me, he robbed me,” those who do not bear ill-will towards this their hatred is appeased.
notes: This is an unexpected formation here, we either have tesaṁ + upasammati giving sandhi tesūpa-, or the locative is being used tesu + upasammati; if it is the former, then we might have expected tesañ-ca sammati, to match the verb in the preceding verse.

pali: Na hi verena verāni sammantīdha kudācanaṁ, averena ca sammanti, esa dhammo sanantano.
english: For not by hatred do hatreds cease at any time in this place, they only cease with non-hatred, this truth is (surely) eternal.
notes: Interestingly an alternative name for what is now known as Hinduism is the sanātana (variant form of sanantana) Dharma; this is the earliest use of the phrase I know of.
This verse and the one that follows do not form a pair, but seem to have been attracted into the collection at this point by word collocation on vera.

pali: Pare ca na vijānanti mayam-ettha yamāmase, ye ca tattha vijānanti tato sammanti medhagā.
english: The others do not understand that we should restrain ourselves here, but (for) those here who do understand, through that, (their) dissensions will cease.
notes: As in verse three the genitive would have made more sense here: yesaṁ tattha vijānanti..., for those who do understand...

pali: Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ, bhojanamhi amattaññuṁ, kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ – taṁ ve pasahati Māro vāto rukkhaṁ va dubbalaṁ.
english: Living contemplating what is pleasant, uncontrolled in sense faculties, not knowing the limit in food, indolent, low in energy – Māra surely overthrows that one, like wind (overthrows) a weak tree.
notes: In the commentary it is clear that viharantaṁ belongs with subhānupassiṁ, not with indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ, as many translations have it. Cf. kāye kāyānupassī viharati, etc. from Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasuttaṁ (DN 22), see elsewhere on this website.

pali: Asubhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu susaṁvutaṁ, bhojanamhi ca mattaññuṁ, saddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ – taṁ ve nappasahati Māro vāto selaṁ va pabbataṁ.
english: Living contemplating the unpleasant, well-controlled in sense faculties, and knowing the limit in food, faithful, with energy aroused – Māra does not overthrow that one, just as wind does not (overthrow) a mountain made of rock.
notes: The form here does not arise through sandhi; na is so closely associated with the verb it is modifying it becomes part of it, as we see frequently with the negative.

pali: Anikkasāvo kāsāvaṁ yo vatthaṁ paridahessati, apeto damasaccena na so kāsāvam-arahati.
english: The one who, while still impure, would wear the renunciant’s robe, unendowed with restraint and truth, is not worthy of the renunciant’s robe.
notes: The form is a double negative, a + nis + kasāva; the word is related is to the one following, the kāsāva, or discoloured robe.

pali: Yo ca vantakasāvassa, sīlesu susamāhito, upeto damasaccena sa ve kāsāvam-arahati.
english: The one who, steady in virtue, throws out (any) impurity, endowed with restraint and truth, is indeed worthy of the renunciant’s robe.
notes: It is unexpected that the opposite form, sīlesu asamāhito, unsteady in virtue, is not found in the corresponding line in the previous verse.

pali: Asāre sāramatino, sāre cāsāradassino, te sāraṁ nādhigacchanti, micchāsaṅkappagocarā.
english: Finding the essential in what is unessential, and seeing the unessential in what is essential, they do not understand what is essential, and resort to wrong intention.
notes: This parses as ca + asāra + dassino; it is not clear to me why ca is found here, as it is not needed by the grammar, the meaning or the metre.

pali: Sārañ-ca sārato ñatvā, asārañ-ca asārato, te sāraṁ adhigacchanti, sammāsaṅkappagocarā.
english: Knowing the essential in what is essential, and the unessential in what is unessential, they understand what is essential, and resort to right intention.
notes: Interesting use of the ablative here, perhaps indicating the starting point.

pali: Yathā agāraṁ ducchannaṁ vuṭṭhī samativijjhati, evaṁ abhāvitaṁ cittaṁ rāgo samativijjhati.
english: Just as the rain penetrates a house with thatching that is poor, so passion penetrates a mind that is undeveloped.

pali: Yathā agāraṁ succhannaṁ vuṭṭhī na samativijjhati, evaṁ subhāvitaṁ cittaṁ rāgo na samativijjhati.
english: Just as rain does not penetrate a house with thatching that is good, so passion cannot penetrate a mind that is well-developed.
notes: This is one of the most perfect of the compositions showing reversal of meaning in the two verses.

pali: Idha socati, pecca socati, pāpakārī ubhayattha socati, so socati, so vihaññati, disvā kammakiliṭṭham-attano.
english: Here he laments, after death he laments, the wicked one laments in both places, he laments, he suffers vexation, seeing the defilement of his own deeds.
notes: Here means here in this world. Idha often has this meaning, just as loke, in the world, often means simply here.
Again this and the following verse, which were probably composed together have been separated by the commentary and given different foundation stories.

pali: Idha modati, pecca modati, katapuñño ubhayattha modati, so modati, so pamodati, disvā kammavisuddhim-attano.
english: Here he rejoices, after death he rejoices, the meritorious one rejoices in both places, he rejoices, he greatly rejoices, seeing the purity of his own deeds.

pali: Idha tappati, pecca tappati, pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati, “Pāpaṁ mĕ katan”-ti tappati, bhiyyo tappati duggatiṁ gato.
english: Here he suffers, after death he suffers, the wicked one suffers in both places, he suffers, thinking: “I have done wickedness,” gone to a bad fate, he suffers much more.
notes: This and the following verse, which again belong together, do not have any parallels in other collections of Dhammapadāni, and may have been composed as variations of the preceding pair of verses.

pali: Idha nandati, pecca nandati, katapuñño ubhayattha nandati, “Puññaṁ mĕ katan”-ti nandati, bhiyyo nandati suggatiṁ gato.
english: Here she is happy, after death she is happy, the righteous one is happy in both places, she is happy, thinking: “I have done merit,” gone to a good fate, she is happy much more.
notes: According to the commentary the verse was spoken about Anāthapiṇḍika’s younger sister.

pali: Bahum-pi ce sahitaṁ bhāsamāno, na takkaro hoti naro pamatto, gopo va gāvo gaṇayaṁ paresaṁ, na bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
english: Even though reciting abundant scriptures, the heedless fellow, who does not do (what they say), like a cowboy counting other’s cattle, does not partake of the ascetic life.
notes: In Sanskrit the g Veda is called saṁhita (a variant form of this word), but according to the commentary sahita means the Tipiṭaka here.
= taṁ kāro, with assimilation.

pali: Appam-pi ce sahitaṁ bhāsamāno, Dhammassa hoti anudhammacārī, rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca pahāya mohaṁ, sammappajāno suvimuttacitto, anupādiyāno idha vā huraṁ vā, sa bhāgavā sāmaññassa hoti.
english: Even though reciting but few scriptures, but living righteously in accordance with Dhamma, abandoning greed, hate and delusion, understanding aright, with mind well-released, that one, unattached here and hereafter, (surely) partakes of the ascetic life.

pali: Appamādo amatapadaṁ, pamādo maccuno padaṁ, appamattā na mīyanti, ye pamattā yathā matā.
english: Heedfulness is the deathless state, heedlessness the state of the dead, the heedful do not die, (but) those who are heedless are as if dead.

pali: Etaṁ visesato ñatvā appamādamhi paṇḍitā, appamāde pamodanti, Ariyānaṁ gocare ratā.
english: The wise, understanding this difference in regard to heedfulness, rejoice in heedfulness, delight in the domain of the Noble Ones.

pali: Te jhāyino sātatikā, niccaṁ daḷhaparakkamā, phusanti dhīrā Nibbānaṁ, yogakkhemaṁ anuttaraṁ.
english: Those who meditate all the time, constant and firm in their effort, those wise ones reach Nibbāna, the unsurpassed release from (all) bonds.

pali: Uṭṭhānavato satīmato, sucikammassa nisammakārino, saññatassa ca Dhammajīvino, appamattassa yasobhivaḍḍhati.
english: For he who is active, mindful, pure in deeds, considerate, self-controlled, living by Dhamma, heedful, fame greatly increases.
notes: The string of genitives in this verse allows us to see side by side some of the different forms the case ending can take: -vato (neuter), -ato (neuter), -assa (masculine) and -ino (masculine).

pali: Uṭṭhānen’ appamādena saṁyamena damena ca, dīpaṁ kayirātha medhāvī yaṁ ogho nābhikīrati.
english: Through activity, heedfulness, through self-control and through restraint, the sage should make an island that no flood waters can overcome.

pali: Pamādam-anuyuñjanti bālā dummedhino janā, appamādañ-ca medhāvī dhanaṁ seṭṭhaṁ va rakkhati.
english: The foolish and stupid people cultivate heedlessness, but the sagacious one guards heedfulness just as his greatest wealth.

pali: Mā pamādam-anuyuñjetha mā kāmaratisanthavaṁ, appamatto hi jhāyanto pappoti vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: Do not cultivate heedlessness, do not be acquainted with delight in sensual pleasure, for the heedful one, meditating, (surely) attains great happiness.

pali: Pamādaṁ appamādena yadā nudati paṇḍito, paññāpāsādam-āruyha, asoko sokiniṁ pajaṁ, pabbataṭṭho va bhummaṭṭhe dhīro bāle avekkhati.
english: When the wise one eliminates heedlessness with his heedfulness, and mounts the palace of wisdom, griefless, (he looks) on grieving people; the wise one, like one standing on a mountain, looks down on the fools, who are standing on the plains.

pali: Appamatto pamattesu, suttesu bahujāgaro, abalassaṁ va sīghasso hitvā, yāti sumedhaso.
english: Heedful amongst the heedless ones, wakeful amongst the ones who sleep, like a swift horse who abandons a weak horse, the true sage moves on.

pali: Appamādena Maghavā devānaṁ seṭṭhataṁ gato, appamādaṁ pasaṁsanti, pamādo garahito sadā.
english: Through heedfulness Maghavā attained leadership of the gods, (the good) praise heedfulness, (but) heedlessness is always blamed.
notes: Maghavā is another name for Sakka, how he became Sakka is told in the commentary. The verse assumes the auditor has some knowledge of the legend, or it may be, that the verse is extracted from the story.

pali: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassivā, saṁyojanaṁ aṇuṁ-thūlaṁ ḍahaṁ aggīva gacchati.
english: A monastic who delights in heedfulness, seeing danger in heedlessness, advances like burning fire against the fetter, small or large.
notes: It is odd that saṁyojanaṁ is singular, where we might have expected a plural, saṁyojanā. The commentary defines it as one of the ten kinds of fetter. The idea is that his heedfulness burns the fetter, as a fire burns and consumes whatever it is attached to. Same at v. 221 below.

pali: Appamādarato bhikkhu, pamāde bhayadassivā, abhabbo parihānāya: Nibbānasseva santike.
english: A monastic who delights in heedfulness, seeing danger in heedlessness, is unable to fall away: he is well-nigh to Nibbāna.
notes: This is the infinitive-like dative, which we also use in English.

pali: Phandanaṁ capalaṁ cittaṁ, dūrakkhaṁ dunnivārayaṁ, ujuṁ karoti medhāvī, usukāro va tejanaṁ.
english: An agitated, unsteady mind, difficult to guard, difficult to ward, the sagacious one makes straight, as a fletcher does his arrow.
notes: In every case in this chapter citta is in the singular, and must mean mind, not thoughts (plural) as many translations have it, which also makes more sense contextually.

pali: Vārijo va thale khitto, oka-m-okata ubbhato, pariphandatidaṁ cittaṁ, Māradheyyaṁ pahātave.
english: Like a fish thrown up on dry land, pulled out from its watery home, the mind is agitated, (one ought) to throw off the sway of Māra.
notes: Oka has both meanings: water and home.

The grammar is not clear here, and words need to be supplied to make good sense, the bold words are added into these translations: Norman: this thought quivers all over in order to escape the dominion of Māra; Carter: This mind flaps; [Fit] to discard [is] Māra’s sway; Burlingame: These thoughts writhe and quiver in their efforts to shake off the power of Māra. I think the ethical force of the verse really demands the imperative interpretation.

pali: Dunniggahassa lahuno yatthakāmanipātino, cittassa damatho sādhu, cittaṁ dantaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
english: * For the mind that is difficult to subdue, flighty, flitting wherever it will, restraint is good, a restrained mind brings happiness.

pali: Sududdasaṁ sunipuṇaṁ yatthakāmanipātinaṁ, cittaṁ rakkhetha medhāvī, cittaṁ guttaṁ sukhāvahaṁ.
english: Hard to see, very subtle, flitting wherever it will, the sage should guard the mind, a guarded mind brings happiness.

pali: Dūraṅgamaṁ ekacaraṁ, asarīraṁ guhāsayaṁ, ye cittaṁ saññam-essanti, mokkhanti Mārabandhanā.
english: * Those who will restrain the mind that roams far, is lonesome, without a body, hidden, gain release from the bonds of Māra.

pali: Anavaṭṭhitacittassa, Saddhammaṁ avijānato, pariplavapasādassa, paññā na paripūrati.
english: For the one with unsettled mind, who does not know the True Dhamma, whose confidence is wavering, wisdom is unfulfilled.

pali: Anavassutacittassa, ananvāhatacetaso, puññapāpapahīnassa natthi jāgarato bhayaṁ.
english: For the one with mind free of lust, for the one with mind unperplexed, for the one who has abandoned making merit and demerit, for the watchful, there is no fear.

pali: Kumbhūpamaṁ kāyam-imaṁ viditvā, nagarūpamaṁ cittam-idaṁ ṭhapetvā, yodhetha Māraṁ paññāvudhena, jitañ-ca rakkhe, anivesano siyā.
english: Knowing this body is (frail) like a jar, establishing the mind like a fortress, fight Māra with the weapon of wisdom, guard your success, and do not be attached.
notes: I.e. is fragile.
Solid and protected.
I do not understand Norman’s translation here of anivesano siyā as: one should take no rest, as nivesana never seems to mean taking a rest.

pali: Aciraṁ vatayaṁ kāyo paṭhaviṁ adhisessati, chuddho apetaviññāṇo, niratthaṁ va kaliṅgaraṁ.
english: Before long has passed by, alas, this body will lie on the ground, rejected, without consciousness, just like a useless piece of wood.
notes: On the ground, or maybe in the ground, but burial was not common, either the body was discarded at the charnel ground, to be taken care of by animals and insects, or it was burned, and sometimes disposed of in bodies of water.

pali: Diso disaṁ yan-taṁ kayirā, verī vā pana verinaṁ – micchāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ pāpiyo naṁ tato kare.
english: Whatever an aggressor might do to an aggressor, or an enemy to an enemy – a mind that is badly-directed can do far worse than that to him.

pali: Na taṁ mātā pitā kayirā, aññe vā pi ca ñātakā, sammāpaṇihitaṁ cittaṁ seyyaso naṁ tato kare.
english: Mother and father might not do for him, or other relatives, as much good as a mind that is well-directed can do for him.
notes: We would better read: Yaṁ taṁ here, whatever Mother and Father and other relatives might do for him.

pali: Kŏ imaṁ paṭhaviṁ vicessati yamalokañ-ca imaṁ sadevakaṁ? Ko dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ kusalo puppham-ivappacessati?
english: Who will know this earth and the lower realm, together with the gods? Who (will reflect) on the well-taught verse of Dhamma as a good man reflects on a flower?
notes: Often translated as overcome, or conquer, as far as I can see the word is unattested with that meaning, unless it be here. Comm: attano ñāṇena vicinissati vijānissati, paṭivijjhissati, sacchikarissati; note the similarity in meaning to pacessati below.
Comm: Yamalokañ-cā ti catubbidhaṃ apāyalokaṁ; Yama’s realm means the fourfold lower realm.
The sentence is evidently meant to encompass the three realms of existence. Norman’s translation here: this world of Yama with its gods is wrong, as there are no gods in the lower realms of course.
Many times translated as gather or pluck, the commentary defines it with: vicinissati vijānissati upaparikkhissati paṭivijjhissati, sacchikarissati.

pali: Sekho paṭhaviṁ vicessati yamalokañ-ca imaṁ sadevakaṁ. Sekho dhammapadaṁ sudesitaṁ kusalo puppham-ivappacessati.
english: The trainee will know this earth and the lower realm, together with the gods. The trainee (will reflect) on the well-taught verse of Dhamma as a good man reflects on a flower.
notes: Sekha is a technical term meaning one who is training, having attained at least to Stream-Entry, but not yet to the final stage of Awakening.

pali: Pheṇūpamaṁ kāyam-imaṁ viditvā, marīcidhammaṁ abhisambudhāno, chetvāna Mārassa papupphakāni, adassanaṁ Maccurājassa gacche.
english: Knowing that this body is just like froth, understanding it has the nature of a mirage, cutting off Māra’s flower-tipped (arrows), one should go beyond the King of Death’s sight.
notes: The emphasis is on its unsubstantiality.
The point here is the illusory nature of permanence.
Or, we might say, Māra’s temptations.
That is, to Nibbāna, which is something beyond the ken of Māra who is the king of death.

pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahogho va, maccu ādāya gacchati.
english: * Death takes up and carries away the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, like a great flood (carries off) a sleeping village.
notes: Here metaphorical for the strands of sense-pleasures (kāmaguṇa). Comm: evaṃ pañcakāmaguṇasaṅkhātāni pupphāni eva pacinantaṃ ... kāmaguṇe byāsattamanasaṃ naraṃ.

pali: Pupphāni heva pacinantaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, atittaṁ yeva kāmesu Antako kurute vasaṁ.
english: * The End-Maker takes control of the one whose mind is attached to collecting flowers, even though he is unsated with sense pleasures.
notes: Antaka, another name for Māra.

pali: Yathā pi bhamaro pupphaṁ vaṇṇagandhaṁ aheṭhayaṁ paḷeti rasam-ādāya, evaṁ gāme munī care.
english: Just as a bee, without hurting the flower, its colour or scent, gathers its nectar and escapes, so should the seer roam in the village.
notes: An interesting choice of words, implying I think that the muni should not only be harmless, but also escape engagement in the village.

pali: Na paresaṁ vilomāni, na paresaṁ katākataṁ attano va avekkheyya, katāni akatāni ca.
english: Not the wrongs of others, or what others have done or have not done one should consider, but what has been done and not done by oneself.
notes: This verse has no mention of flowers, or anything similar, and also does not seem to be connected by word collocation, so its inclusion here is rather a mystery.

pali: Yamakavaggo Paṭhamo Related Verses from the Dhammapada Yathā pi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ vaṇṇavantaṁ agandhakaṁ, evaṁ subhāsitā vācā aphalā hoti akubbato.
english: The Chapter about the Pairs, the First Just like a beautiful flower, which has colour, but lacks fragrance, so are well-spoken words fruitless for the one who acts not (on them).

pali: Yathā pi ruciraṁ pupphaṁ vaṇṇavantaṁ sagandhakaṁ, evaṁ subhāsitā vācā saphalā hoti pakubbato.
english: Just like a beautiful flower, which has colour, and has fragrance, so are well-spoken words fruitful for the one who does act (on them).

pali: Yathā pi puppharāsimhā kayirā mālāguṇe bahū, evaṁ jātena maccena kattabbaṁ kusalaṁ bahuṁ.
english: Just as from a heap of flowers one might make a lot of garlands, so should many good deeds be done by one who is born a mortal.

pali: Na pupphagandho paṭivātam-eti, na candanaṁ tagaramallikā vā, satañ-ca gandho paṭivātam-eti, sabbā disā sappuriso pavāyati.
english: The fragrance of flowers goes not against the wind, nor does sandalwood or pinwheel or white jasmine, but the fragrance of the good goes against the wind, the true person’s (fragrance) permeates all directions.
notes: Meaning his virtue.

pali: Candanaṁ tagaraṁ vā pi, uppalaṁ atha vassikī, etesaṁ gandhajātānaṁ sīlagandho anuttaro.
english: Sandalwood, pinwheel, then water lily and striped jasmine, amongst these kinds of fragrance virtue’s fragrance is unsurpassed.

pali: Appamatto ayaṁ gandho yāyaṁ tagaracandanī, yo ca sīlavataṁ gandho vāti devesu uttamo.
english: Pinwheel and sandalwood fragrance are insignificant, but the fragrance of one who has virtue flutters supreme amongst the gods.
notes: Vāti means both blow, flutter and weave, and in the commentarial story Sakka takes the form of a weaver.

pali: Tesaṁ sampannasīlānaṁ, appamādavihārinaṁ, sammad-aññāvimuttānaṁ, Māro maggaṁ na vindati.
english: * Māra cannot find the path of those endowed with virtue, who live heedfully, and who are freed through complete and deep knowledge.
notes: This is a common simile in the discourses also, as Māra can only find what is still inside the rounds of birth and death.
Again this verse has no connection to flowers, there may be word-collocation on sīla in the previous verse attracting into this position.

pali: Yathā saṅkāradhānasmiṁ ujjhitasmiṁ mahāpathe padumaṁ tattha jāyetha, sucigandhaṁ manoramaṁ,
english: Just as in a forsaken and discarded heap along the highway a lotus might arise in that place, with a pure fragrance, delighting the mind,
notes: Jāyetha is 3rd singular optative in the middle voice.

pali: evaṁ saṅkārabhūtesu, andhabhūte puthujjane atirocati paññāya Sammāsambuddhasāvako.
english: * so amongst the forsaken, the Perfect Sambuddha’s disciple outshines the blind and ordinary folk through his wisdom.
notes: The verse lacks the symmetry we might expect.

pali: Dīghā jāgarato ratti, dīghaṁ santassa yojanaṁ, dīgho bālānaṁ saṁsāro Saddhammaṁ avijānataṁ.
english: Long is the night for one awake, long is a league for one tired, long is the round of births and deaths for fools who know not True Dhamma.
notes: The similes do not quite match the statement, nights feel long, leagues feel long, but the continuance in saṁsāra actually is long for a fool. The verse provides a good illustration of how adjectives, here dīgha, adapt to the nouns they qualify: ratti, feminine; yojana, neut, and saṁsāra, masculine.

pali: Carañ-ce nādhigaccheyya seyyaṁ sadisam-attano, ekacariyaṁ daḷhaṁ kayirā: natthi bāle sahāyatā.
english: If while roaming one cannot find one better or the same as oneself, one should resolve to go alone: there is no friendship with fools.
notes: Although this does express a common Buddhist sentiment, we should remember that in the early Tuvaṭakasuttaṁ of the Aṭṭhakavagga (Sn 4, XIV vs. 4), we are cautioned about thinking of others as better, the same or worse than ourselves.

pali: “Puttā matthi, dhanam-matthi,” iti bālo vihaññati, attā hi attano natthi, kuto puttā, kuto dhanaṁ?
english: “Sons are mine, riches are mine,” so the fool suffers vexation, when even self is not his own, how then sons, how then riches?
notes: This parses as me atthi.
If his self was really his, he would have control over it, and be able to say: let this body be thus, let it not be thus, but he cannot (see Anattalakkhaṇasuttaṁ).

pali: Yo bālo maññati bālyaṁ, paṇḍito vāpi tena so, bālo ca paṇḍitamānī, sa ve bālo ti vuccati.
english: The fool who knows (his) foolishness, is at least wise in that (matter), the fool who is proud of his wisdom, he is said to be a fool indeed.

pali: Yāvajīvam-pi ce bālo paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati, na so Dhammaṁ vijānāti, dabbī sūparasaṁ yathā.
english: Even if a fool attends on a wise man for his whole life long, he does not learn Dhamma, just as spoon learns not the taste of curry.

pali: Muhuttam-api ce viññū paṇḍitaṁ payirupāsati, khippaṁ Dhammaṁ vijānāti, jivhā sūparasaṁ yathā.
english: If a perceptive man attends on a wise man even for a second, he quickly learns Dhamma, just as the tongue (learns) the taste of curry.

pali: Caranti bālā dummedhā amitteneva attanā, karontā pāpakaṁ kammaṁ, yaṁ hoti kaṭukapphalaṁ.
english: Stupid fools live having themselves as their own foes, committing wicked deeds, which produce bitter fruit.

pali: Na taṁ kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā anutappati, yassa assumukho rodaṁ, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
english: That deed is not well done, which, having done, one has regret, for which he has tears on his face, as the result follows him round.

pali: Tañ-ca kammaṁ kataṁ sādhu, yaṁ katvā nānutappati, yassa patīto sumano, vipākaṁ paṭisevati.
english: But that deed is well done, which, having done, one has no regret, for which he is pleased and happy, as the result follows him round.

pali: Madhuvā maññati bālo, yāva pāpaṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ, bālo dukkhaṁ nigacchati.
english: The fool thinks it sweet, as long as the wicked deed does not ripen, but when the wicked deed ripens, the fool undergoes suffering.

pali: Māse māse kusaggena bālo bhuñjetha bhojanaṁ, na so saṅkhātadhammānaṁ kalaṁ agghati soḷasiṁ.
english: From month to month the fool may eat food with the tip of kusa-grass, (but) he is not worth a sixteenth part of those who have mastered Dhamma.
notes: Meaning he may be an ascetic engaging in very strict practices, such as eating very little.

pali: Na hi pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ, sajju khīraṁ va muccati, ḍahantaṁ bālam-anveti, bhasmacchanno va pāvako.
english: A wicked deed that has been done, like milk, does not turn all at once, smouldering, it follows the fool, like a fire covered with ashes.
notes: Ḍahati means burns, smoulders, consumes, torments; it is hard to get the force of it over in natural English.
There is a mix of similes in this verse, which don’t fit well together.

pali: Yāvad-eva anatthāya ñattaṁ bālassa jāyati, hanti bālassa sukkaṁsaṁ, muddham-assa vipātayaṁ.
english: As far as learning arises for a fool, it is only to his disadvantage, it destroys the fool’s good fortune, and it will destroy his head.
notes: The commentary explains that his head here means his wisdom, though it would have been easy to write paññam-assa vipātayaṁ if that was what was intended.

pali: Asataṁ bhāvanam-iccheyya, purekkhārañ-ca bhikkhusu, āvāsesu ca issariyaṁ, pūjā parakulesu ca:
english: He may wish for the respect that is lacking, and status amongst the monastics, for control in the living quarters, and worship amongst good families:

pali: “Mameva kata’ maññantu gihī pabbajitā ubho, mameva ativasā assu, kiccākiccesu kismici”, iti bālassa saṅkappo, icchā māno ca vaḍḍhati.
english: “Householders and renunciants should both think this was done by me, let them (all) be under my sway, in all to be done and not done”, so does the fool think, (meanwhile) his desires and conceit increase.

pali: Aññā hi lābhūpanisā, aññā Nibbānagāminī, evam-etaṁ abhiññāya bhikkhu Buddhassa sāvako sakkāraṁ nābhinandeyya, vivekam-anubrūhaye.
english: For the means to gains is one thing, the (path) going to Nibbāna another, thus knowing this the monastic disciple of the Buddha should not delight in honours, (but) practise in solitude.
notes: Again the verse lacks any mention of fools, and might have been better placed in the Bhikkhuvagga.

pali: Nidhīnaṁ va pavattāraṁ yaṁ passe vajjadassinaṁ, niggayhavādiṁ medhāviṁ tādisaṁ paṇḍitaṁ bhaje; tādisaṁ bhajamānassa seyyo hoti na pāpiyo.
english: One should regard someone who shows your faults just like one who points out hidden treasure, one should keep company with such a sagacious, learned person who reproves you; keeping company with such is (surely) better for you, not worse.

pali: Ovadeyyānusāseyya, asabbhā ca nivāraye, sataṁ hi so piyo hoti, asataṁ hoti appiyo.
english: One should advise and instruct, and forbid whatever is vile, for he is dear to the good, (but) he is not dear to the bad.
notes: Although the theme of the good person is present, neither this verse nor the next mention the paṇḍita.

pali: Na bhaje pāpake mitte, na bhaje purisādhame, bhajetha mitte kalyāṇe, bhajetha purisuttame.
english: One should not keep company with wicked friends, one should not keep company with the ignoble, you should keep company with spiritual friends, you should keep company with superior people.
notes: This is a bit irregular: the first two lines are in the 3rd person singular, and the second two in the 2nd person (polite) plural. It is possible we should take the last two lines as being in middle voice, but it would have been easy to write bhajeyya if the change of person wasn’t intended. Patna reads bhajetha throughout, and Udānavarga reads bhaje, probably trying to regularise the reading.

pali: Dhammapīti sukhaṁ seti, vippasannena cetasā, Ariyappavedite Dhamme sadā ramati paṇḍito.
english: The one who drinks Dhamma lives well, with a clear mind, the wise one will always delight in the Dhamma that is made known by the Noble.
notes: Comm: Dhammapayako Dhammaṁ pivanto ti attho... ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhanto; the one who makes (others) drink Dhamma, who drinks Dhamma... who experiences the Noble truths. It seems both causative and active meanings may be intended.

pali: Udakaṁ hi nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ, dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, attānaṁ damayanti paṇḍitā.
english: Course-makers lead water, fletchers straighten arrows, carpenters straighten wood, the wise master themselves.
notes: For a variant of this verse, see 145 below.

pali: Selo yathā ekaghano vātena na samīrati, evaṁ nindāpasaṁsāsu na samiñjanti paṇḍitā.
english: Just as solid rock is not shaken by the wind, so the wise are not moved by blame or praise.

pali: Yathā pi rahado gambhīro vippasanno anāvilo, evaṁ Dhammāni sutvāna vippasīdanti paṇḍitā.
english: Like a lake that is deep, clear and unruffled, just so the wise are confident after listening to Dhamma.
notes: There is a play on meaning of the forms derived from vippasīdati, it means both clear and confident.

pali: Sabbattha ve sappurisā cajanti, na kāmakāmā lapayanti santo; sukhena phuṭṭhā atha vā dukhena, noccāvacaṁ paṇḍitā dassayanti.
english: True people surely everywhere renounce, the good do not talk of desiring sense-pleasures; when touched by pleasure or by suffering, the wise show neither elation or depression.

pali: Na attahetu na parassa hetu, na puttam-icche na dhanaṁ na raṭṭhaṁ – na iccheyya adhammena samiddhim-attano; sa sīlavā paññavā dhammiko siyā.
english: Not for one’s own sake and not for another’s sake, not desiring a child, riches, or a kingdom – he should not desire his success through corruption; he should be both virtuous and wise and righteous.
notes: Through wrong, unrighteous or corrupt ways.

pali: Appakā te manussesu ye janā pāragāmino, athāyaṁ itarā pajā tīram-evānudhāvati,
english: Amongst humans few people go beyond, the rest of the people run down the bank,

pali: ye ca kho sammad-akkhāte Dhamme dhammānuvattino, te janā pāram-essanti, maccudheyyaṁ suduttaraṁ.
english: but those who live righteously, conforming with this well-taught Dhamma, those folk will go beyond the realm of death, which is very hard to cross.
notes: There is no mention of paṇḍita in this verse, the closest being those who live righteously.

pali: Kaṇhaṁ dhammaṁ vippahāya, sukkaṁ bhāvetha paṇḍito, okā anokaṁ āgamma; viveke yattha dūramaṁ,
english: Having abandoned the dark state, the wise one should develop the bright, having gone forth to homelessness from home; in solitude, where it is hard to delight.

pali: Tatrābhiratim-iccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano, pariyodapeyya attānaṁ cittaklesehi paṇḍito.
english: One should desire to delight in that place, having given up sense pleasures, and having no possessions, the wise one should purify the self of defilements of mind.

pali: Yesaṁ sambodhi-aṅgesu sammā cittaṁ subhāvitaṁ, ādānapaṭinissagge anupādāya ye ratā, khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā.
english: For those who have well developed with right mind the factors of complete awakening, having given up grasping, those who delight in being unattached, pollutant-free, shining forth, are emancipated in the world.

pali: Gataddhino visokassa vippamuttassa sabbadhi, sabbaganthappahīnassa, pariḷāho na vijjati.
english: For the one who has reached his goal, who grieves not, being released on all sides, who has abandoned all the knots, no consuming fever is found.
notes: Usually enumerated as four: abhijjhā-, byāpāda-, sīlabbataparāmāsa-, idaṁsaccābhinivesagantha;the knots of avarice, ill-will, grasping at virtue and practices, and inclination to (insisting that) ‘this is the truth’.
Passion is the consuming fever which is implied here.

pali: Uyyuñjanti satīmanto na nikete ramanti te, haṁsā va pallalaṁ hitvā, okam-okaṁ jahanti te.
english: The mindful ones who are striving do not delight in a dwelling, like geese who abandon a lake, they abandon fondness for homes.
notes: It is hard to get across all the double meanings in this verse, but niketa means: home, company and attachment; and oka means water, home and attachment.

pali: Yesaṁ sannicayo natthi, ye pariññātabhojanā, suññato animitto ca vimokkho yesa’ gocaro, ākāse va sakuntānaṁ, gati tesaṁ durannayā.
english: For those who have no stores, those who comprehend food aright, for those whose resort is the liberation that is empty or signless, like the birds in the sky, their track is hard to find.
notes: The commentary defines this as having stores of kamma, which would lead to rebirth; the Arahat of course has no such stores.
Seeing its disgusting nature.
This is a reference to the three liberations (vimokkha), which are defined as being signless (animitta), desireless (apanihita) and empty (suññatā). The second is implied, rather than stated here.
Gati may mean their course, track or destiny; it means that they cannot be known either in this world, or when gone beyond.

pali: Yassāsavā parikkhīṇā, āhāre ca anissito, suññato animitto ca vimokkho yassa gocaro, ākāse va sakuntānaṁ, padaṁ tassa durannayaṁ.
english: For him whose pollutants are destroyed, who is not dependent on the foods, for him whose resort is the liberation that is empty or signless, like the birds in the sky, his footprint is hard to find.
notes: The commentary says it means the foods of craving and views.
Pada may mean his footprint or his state; again it means that they cannot be known either in this world, or when gone beyond

pali: Yassindriyāni samathaṁ gatāni, assā yathā sārathinā sudantā, pahīnamānassa anāsavassa – devā pi tassa pihayanti tādino.
english: For the one whose senses are stilled, like horses well-trained by their charioteer, who has abandoned conceit, who is without pollutants – even the gods envy such a one.

pali: Paṭhavisamo no virujjhati, indakhīlūpamŏ tādi subbato, rahado va apetakaddamo – saṁsārā na bhavanti tādino.
english: One untroubled just like the earth, steadfast just like a city-post, like a lake mud-free – such a one continues not in births and deaths.

pali: Santaṁ tassa manaṁ hoti, santā vācā ca kamma’ ca, sammad-aññāvimuttassa, upasantassa tādino.
english: His mind is calm, his speech and his actions are also calm, liberated by right knowledge, such a one is (truly) peaceful.

pali: Assaddho akataññū ca sandhicchedo ca yo naro, hatāvakāso vantāso, sa ve uttamaporiso.
english: The person who is beyond (mere) faith, who knows that which is unmade, who has cut off (rebirth-)linking, who has destroyed the occasion, who has thrown out hope and desire, is surely the person supreme.
notes: Because he has seen the truth for himself.
Nibbāna.
Sandhi here is short for paṭisandhi, rebirth-linking.
Destroyed the occasion for good and bad deeds.
Āsa, hope, desire, is here a synonym for craving.

pali: Gāme vā yadi vāraññe, ninne vā yadi vā thale, yattharahanto viharanti, taṁ bhūmiṁ rāmaṇeyyakaṁ.
english: Whether in the village or wilds, whether on low or on high ground, wherever the Arahats live, that ground is (surely) delightful.
notes: This is the only verse in this chapter which actually speaks of Arahats.

pali: Ramaṇīyāni araññāni yattha na ramatī jano, vītarāgā ramissanti, na te kāmagavesino.
english: The delightful wildernesses where the people do not delight, those without passion will take delight, (but) not those who seek sense pleasures.

pali: Sahassam-api ce vācā anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ atthapadaṁ seyyo yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
english: Though there are a thousand sayings consisting of useless words, better is one useful word hearing which one is brought to peace.

pali: Sahassam-api ce gāthā anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ gāthāpadaṁ seyyo yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
english: Though there are a thousand verses consisting of useless words, better is one word of a verse hearing which one is brought to peace.

pali: Yo ce gāthāsataṁ bhāse anatthapadasaṁhitā, ekaṁ Dhammapadaṁ seyyo, yaṁ sutvā upasammati.
english: One may speak a hundred verses consisting of useless words, better is one verse of Dhamma, hearing which one is brought to peace.

pali: Yo sahassaṁ sahassena saṅgāme mānuse jine, ekañ-ca jeyya attānaṁ, sa ve saṅgāmajuttamo.
english: One may conquer a thousand men a thousand times in a battle, but having conquered one’s own self, one would surely be supreme in battle.

pali: Attā have jitaṁ seyyo yā cāyaṁ itarā pajā, attadantassa posassa, niccaṁ saññatacārino,
english: Conquest over self is better than that over other people, for the person who conquers himself, who lives constantly well-restrained,

pali: neva devo na gandhabbo, na Māro saha Brahmunā, jitaṁ apajitaṁ kayirā tathārūpassa jantuno.
english: neither gods, nor gandhabbas, nor Māra together with Brahmās, can turn conquest into defeat for a person who is like this.

pali: Māse māse sahassena yo yajetha sataṁ samaṁ; ekañ-ca bhāvitattānaṁ muhuttam-api pūjaye – sā yeva pūjanā seyyo yañ-ce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
english: One might give alms impartially with a thousand (coins of money) month by month for a hundred (years); and one might worship someone with developed self for a second – that worship is surely better than the hundred-year sacrifice.
notes: Other translations seem to take samaṁ as meaning year, perhaps following the paraphrase in the commentary; however, it doesn’t seem to be attested in that meaning, and the singular number would be wrong, both of which are against it. Rather is seems we should take it as an adjective with the meaning, equally, indifferently, impartially.
The commentary says it means anyone who is a Noble Person or one who has attained any of the four stages of Awakening.

pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jantu aggiṁ paricare vane; ekañ-ca bhāvitattānaṁ muhuttam-api pūjaye – sā yeva pūjanā seyyo yañ-ce vassasataṁ hutaṁ.
english: One person might care for the fire in the woods for a hundred years; and one might worship someone with developed self for a second – that worship is surely better than the hundred-year sacrifice.

pali: Yaṁ kiñci yiṭṭhaṁ ca hutaṁ ca loke saṁvaccharaṁ yajetha puññapekkho, sabbam-pi taṁ na catubhāgam-eti – abhivādanā ujjugatesu seyyo.
english: Whatever the alms or the sacrifice in the world the one seeking merit may give for a year, all that comes not to a quarter (of the merit) – better is the worship of the upright.

pali: Abhivādanasīlissa niccaṁ vaddhāpacāyino, cattāro dhammā vaḍḍhanti: āyu vaṇṇo sukhaṁ balaṁ.
english: For the one who is constantly worshipping honourable elders, four things increase: the length of life, beauty, happiness, and strength.

pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, dussīlo asamāhito, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, sīlavantassa jhāyino.
english: One might live for a hundred years, unvirtuous and uncomposed, (but) a life of one day is better, for one with virtue and meditation.

pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, duppañño asamāhito, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, paññavantassa jhāyino.
english: One might live for a hundred years, lacking in wisdom, uncomposed, (but) a life of one day is better, for one endowed with wisdom and meditation.

pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve, kusīto hīnavīriyo, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo, viriyam-ārabhato daḷhaṁ.
english: One might live for a hundred years, indolent, with less energy, (but) a life of one day is better, for one with energy set up and firm.

pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ udayabbayaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato udayabbayaṁ.
english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing rise and fall, (but) a life of one day is better (for the one) seeing rise and fall.

pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ amataṁ padaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato amataṁ padaṁ.
english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing the deathless state, (but) a life of one day is better (for one) seeing the deathless state.

pali: Yo ca vassasataṁ jīve apassaṁ dhammam-uttamaṁ, ekāhaṁ jīvitaṁ seyyo passato dhammam-uttamaṁ.
english: One might live for a hundred years without seeing the supreme state, (but) a life of one day is better (for one) seeing the supreme state.

pali: Abhittharetha kalyāṇe, pāpā cittaṁ nivāraye, dandhaṁ hi karato puññaṁ pāpasmiṁ ramatī mano.
english: Hasten to do wholesome deeds, ward off the mind from wickedness, for the mind of the one slow in merit delights in wickedness.

pali: Pāpañ-ce puriso kayirā, na taṁ kayirā punappunaṁ, na tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, dukkho pāpassa uccayo.
english: Should a person do that which is wicked, he should not do it again and again, let him not place his intention in it, (for) there is an accumulation of suffering for the wicked one.

pali: Puññañ-ce puriso kayirā, kayirāthetaṁ punappunaṁ, tamhi chandaṁ kayirātha, sukho puññassa uccayo.
english: If a person should make merit, he should do it again and again, let him place his intention there, there is an increase of happiness for the one who has made merit.

pali: Pāpo pi passati bhadraṁ yāva pāpaṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati pāpaṁ atha pāpo pāpāni passati.
english: Even the wicked one experiences good fortune while the wickedness does not ripen, but when the wickedness ripens then the wicked one experiences wicked things.

pali: Bhadro pi passati pāpaṁ yāva bhadraṁ na paccati, yadā ca paccati bhadraṁ atha bhadro bhadrāni passati.
english: Even the fortunate one experiences wickedness as long as the good fortune does not ripen, but when the fortune ripens then the fortunate one experiences good fortune.

pali: Māppamaññetha pāpassa: na maṁ taṁ āgamissati, udabindunipātena udakumbho pi pūrati, bālo pūrati pāpassa, thokaṁ thokam-pi ācinaṁ.
english: One should not despise a little wickedness (thinking): it will not come to me, through the falling of water drops the water-pot is (quickly) filled, the fool, gathering bit by bit, becomes full of wickedness.

pali: Māppamaññetha puññassa: na maṁ taṁ āgamissati. udabindunipātena udakumbho pi pūrati, dhīro pūrati puññassa, thokathokam-pi ācinaṁ.
english: One should not despise a little merit (thinking): it will not come to me, through the falling of water drops the water-pot is (quickly) filled, the wise one, gathering bit by bit, becomes full of merit.

pali: Vāṇijo va bhayaṁ maggaṁ, appasattho mahaddhano, visaṁ jīvitukāmo va, pāpāni parivajjaye.
english: Like a merchant on a fearful path, with few friends and great wealth, as one loving life (would avoid) poison, (so) should one avoid wicked deeds.

pali: Pāṇimhi ce vaṇo nāssa hareyya pāṇinā visaṁ, nābbaṇaṁ visam-anveti, natthi pāpaṁ akubbato.
english: If there is no wound in his hand he can carry poison with his hand, poison does not enter without a wound, there is no bad result for the one who does no (wrong).

pali: So appaduṭṭhassa narassa dussati, suddhassa posassa anaṅgaṇassa, tam-eva bālaṁ pacceti pāpaṁ, sukhumo rajo paṭivātaṁ va khitto.
english: One offends against the inoffensive one, a purified and passionless person, that wicked deed (then) returns to the fool, like fine dust that is thrown against the wind.

pali: Gabbham-eke ’papajjanti, nirayaṁ pāpakammino, saggaṁ sugatino yanti, parinibbanti anāsavā.
english: Some are reborn in the womb, (but) those who are wicked in the underworld, the righteous go to heaven, those who are pollutant-free are emancipated.

pali: Na antalikkhe, na samuddamajjhe, na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa: na vijjatī so jagatippadeso yatthaṭṭhito mucceyya pāpakammā.
english: Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor after entering a mountain cleft: there is no place found on this earth where one can be free from (the results of) wicked deeds.

pali: Na antalikkhe, na samuddamajjhe, na pabbatānaṁ vivaraṁ pavissa: na vijjatī so jagatippadeso, yatthaṭṭhitaṁ nappasahetha maccu.
english: Neither in the sky, nor in the middle of the ocean, nor after entering a mountain cleft: there is no place found on this earth, in which death does not overcome one.

pali: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbe bhāyanti maccuno, attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
english: Everyone trembles at the stick, everyone is in fear of death, comparing oneself (with others), one should not hurt or have (them) hurt.

pali: Sabbe tasanti daṇḍassa, sabbesaṁ jīvitaṁ piyaṁ, attānaṁ upamaṁ katvā, na haneyya na ghātaye.
english: Everyone trembles at the stick, for all of them life is dear, comparing oneself (with others), one should not hurt or have (them) hurt.

pali: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni yo daṇḍena vihiṁsati, attano sukham-esāno, pecca so na labhate sukhaṁ.
english: One who harms with a stick beings who desire happiness, while seeking happiness for himself, won’t find happiness after death.

pali: Sukhakāmāni bhūtāni yo daṇḍena na hiṁsati, attano sukham-esāno, pecca so labhate sukhaṁ.
english: One who harms not with a stick beings who desire happiness, while seeking happiness for himself, will find happiness after death.

pali: Māvoca pharusaṁ kañci, vuttā paṭivadeyyu’ taṁ, dukkhā hi sārambhakathā, paṭidaṇḍā phuseyyu’ taṁ.
english: Do not say anything harsh, spoken to they might answer back to you, for arrogant talk entails misery, and they might strike you back with a stick.

pali: Sace neresi attānaṁ kaṁso upahato yathā, esa pattosi Nibbānaṁ, sārambho te na vijjati.
english: If you make no sound like a gong that is broken, you are (like) one who has attained Nibbāna, contention is not found in you.

pali: Yathā daṇḍena gopālo gāvo pāceti gocaraṁ, evaṁ jarā ca maccu ca āyuṁ pācenti pāṇinaṁ.
english: Like a cowherd with a stick drives cattle to pasture, so do old age and death drive life out of beings.

pali: Atha pāpāni kammāni karaṁ bālo na bujjhati, sehi kammehi dummedho aggidaḍḍho va tappati.
english: The fool does not understand the wicked deeds he is doing, the stupid one is consumed by his deeds as (by) a burning fire.

pali: Yo daṇḍena adaṇḍesu appaduṭṭhesu dussati dasannam-aññataraṁ ṭhānaṁ khippam-eva nigacchati:
english: Whoever offends with a stick those who are inoffensive and harmless will quickly fall into one of ten states:

pali: vedanaṁ pharusaṁ, jāniṁ, sarīrassa ca bhedanaṁ, garukaṁ vā pi ābādhaṁ, cittakkhepaṁ va pāpuṇe,
english: harsh feelings, loss (of his wealth), and the break up of the body, or even heavy affliction, or surely he will lose his mind,

pali: rājato vā upassaggaṁ, abbhakkhānaṁ va dāruṇaṁ, parikkhayaṁ va ñātīnaṁ, bhogānaṁ va pabhaṅguraṁ,
english: (there may be) danger from the King, or slander that is terrible, (he may suffer from) loss of kin, or (from) the destruction of wealth,

pali: atha vāssa agārāni aggi ḍahati pāvako, kāyassa bhedā duppañño nirayaṁ so upapajjati.
english: also his houses may be consumed by flames and fire, and at the break-up of the body that one lacking in wisdom will arise in the underworld.

pali: Na naggacariyā na jaṭā na paṅkā, nānāsakā thaṇḍilasāyikā vā, rājo ca jallaṁ ukkuṭikappadhānaṁ, sodhenti maccaṁ avitiṇṇakaṅkhaṁ.
english: Not going naked, nor matted hair, nor mud, nor fasting or lying on stony ground, dust and dirt, (or) striving while squatting, can purify a mortal who has not removed uncertainty.
notes: There seems to be no particular reason this is in the Chapter about the Stick.

pali: Alaṅkato ce pi samaṁ careyya, santo danto niyato brahmacārī, sabbesu bhūtesu nidhāya daṇḍaṁ, so brāhmaṇo so samaṇo sa bhikkhu.
english: Even if he were to adorn himself, (but) is peaceful, trained, settled, spiritual, and has put aside the stick towards all beings, he is a brahmin, an ascetic, a monastic.
notes: This could also be translated as has put aside violence towards all beings.

pali: Hirīnisedho puriso koci lokasmi’ vijjati, yo nindaṁ appabodhati, asso bhadro kasām-iva.
english: Whatever person in the world is found restrained by conscience, and is aware of his fault, is like a good horse that is (restrained) by a whip.

pali: Asso yathā bhadro kasāniviṭṭho, ātāpino saṁvegino bhavātha. Saddhāya sīlena ca vīriyena ca, samādhinā Dhammavinicchayena ca. Sampannavijjācaraṇā patissatā, pahassatha dukkham-idaṁ anappakaṁ.
english: Like a good horse restrained by the whip, you should be ardent and spiritually intense. Having faith, virtue and energy, concentration and investigation of the Dhamma. One who has understanding and good conduct, mindfulness, will abandon this not insignificant suffering.
notes: Again these two verses have no connection to a stick, but also do not fit in thematically with any other chapter either.

pali: Udakaṁ hi nayanti nettikā, usukārā namayanti tejanaṁ, dāruṁ namayanti tacchakā, attānaṁ damayanti subbatā.
english: Course-makers lead water, fletchers straighten arrows, carpenters straighten wood, the mild master themselves.
notes: For a variant of this verse, see verse 80 above.

pali: Ko nu hāso, kim-ānando, niccaṁ pajjalite sati, andhakārena onaddhā, padīpaṁ na gavesatha?
english: Why this laughter, why this joy, when the world is constantly burning, why, when enveloped by darkness, do you not seek for a light?

pali: Passa cittakataṁ bimbaṁ, arukāyaṁ samussitaṁ, āturaṁ bahusaṅkappaṁ, yassa natthi dhuvaṁ ṭhiti.
english: See this beautified manikin, a heap of sores that is raised up, sick, imagined in many ways, which has nothing stable or firm.
notes: It is very unclear how we should read this, as we are talking about the body it seems translations indicating it has many intentions are incorrect. The comm. says: mahājanena bahudhā saṅkappaṁ, which I follow.

pali: Parijiṇṇam-idaṁ rūpaṁ, roganīḷaṁ pabhaṅguraṁ, bhijjati pūtisandeho, maraṇantaṁ hi jīvitaṁ.
english: This body is worn out, a nest of disease, perishing, the putrid body comes to destruction, for life ends in death.

pali: Yānimāni apatthāni alāpūneva sārade kāpotakāni aṭṭhīni, tāni disvāna kā rati?
english: Like discarded white gourds thrown away in autumn are these grey bones; seeing them, why is there delight?
notes: The comm. positions the Buddha as pointing out discarded corpses as he says this; the word specifically means white gourds.

pali: Aṭṭhīnaṁ nagaraṁ kataṁ, maṁsalohitalepanaṁ, yattha jarā ca maccu ca, māno makkho ca ohito.
english: This fortress is made out of bones, plastered over with flesh and blood, but hidden within lie old age, death, also conceit and anger.
notes: It seems strange to say that the mental states of conceit and anger lie hidden in the body here.

pali: Jīranti ve rājarathā sucittā, atho sarīram-pi jaraṁ upeti, satañ-ca Dhammo na jaraṁ upeti, santo have sabbhi pavedayanti.
english: Decorated royal chariots decay, and the body also decays, but the good Dhamma does not decay, the good surely pass it on to the good.

pali: Appassutāyaṁ puriso balivaddo va jīrati, maṁsāni tassa vaḍḍhanti, paññā tassa na vaḍḍhati.
english: The person of little learning increases in age like an ox, (for although) his flesh does increase, his wisdom does not increase.

pali: Anekajātisaṁsāraṁ sandhāvissaṁ anibbisaṁ gahakārakaṁ gavesanto: dukkhā jāti punappunaṁ.
english: Through the round of countless births and deaths I have wandered without finding the housebuilder I was seeking: born and suffering once again.

pali: Gahakāraka diṭṭhosi! Puna gehaṁ na kāhasi: sabbā te phāsukā bhaggā, gahakūṭaṁ visaṅkhitaṁ, visaṅkhāragataṁ cittaṁ, taṇhānaṁ khayam-ajjhagā.
english: O housebuilder, now you are seen! You will not build the house again: all your rafters have been broken, and the ridgepole has been destroyed, my mind has reached the unconditioned, and craving’s end has been achieved.

pali: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ, aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ, jiṇṇakoñcā ca jhāyanti khīṇamacche va pallale.
english: Not having lived the holy life, not having gained wealth in their youth, they waste away like herons in a small lake devoid of fish.

pali: Acaritvā brahmacariyaṁ aladdhā yobbane dhanaṁ senti cāpātikhittā va, purāṇāni anutthunaṁ.
english: Not having lived the holy life, not having gained wealth in their youth, they lie like (shafts) shot from a bow, wailing about things in the past.

pali: Attānañ-ce piyaṁ jaññā rakkheyya naṁ surakkhitaṁ, tiṇṇam-aññataraṁ yāmaṁ paṭijaggeyya paṇḍito.
english: If one regards oneself as dear one should guard oneself right well, during one of the three watches (of the night) the wise one should stay alert.

pali: Attānam-eva paṭhamaṁ patirūpe nivesaye, athaññam-anusāseyya, na kilisseyya paṇḍito.
english: First one should establish oneself in what is suitable, then one can advise another, the wise one should not have (any) defilement.

pali: Attānañ-ce tathā kayirā yathaññam-anusāsati, sudanto vata dametha, attā hi kira duddamo.
english: He should do himself as he would advise another (to do), being well-trained, he could surely train (another), for it is said the self is difficult to train.

pali: Attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā? Attanā va sudantena nāthaṁ labhati dullabhaṁ.
english: For the self is the friend of self, for what other friend would there be? When the self is well-trained, one finds a friend that is hard to find.

pali: Attanā va kataṁ pāpaṁ, attajaṁ attasambhavaṁ, abhimatthati dummedhaṁ vajiraṁ vasmamayaṁ maṇiṁ.
english: That wickedness done by oneself, born in oneself, arising in oneself, crushes the one who is stupid, as a diamond (crushes) a rock-jewel.

pali: Yassa accantadussīlyaṁ, māluvā Sālam-ivotataṁ, karoti so tathattānaṁ yathā naṁ icchatī diso.
english: The one who has an exceeding lack of virtue, like a deadly creeper covering a Sal tree, makes himself the same as his enemy wishes him to be.

pali: Sukarāni asādhūni, attano ahitāni ca, yaṁ ve hitañ-ca sādhuñ-ca taṁ ve paramadukkaraṁ.
english: Easily done are things not good, and unbeneficial for oneself, but that which is beneficial and good is supremely hard to do.

pali: Yo sāsanaṁ arahataṁ Ariyānaṁ Dhammajīvinaṁ paṭikkosati dummedho diṭṭhiṁ nissāya pāpikaṁ, phalāni kaṭṭhakasseva attaghaññāya phallati.
english: * Whoever reviles the worthy teaching of the Noble Ones who live by Dhamma, that stupid one, depending on wicked views, like the bamboo when it bears fruit, brings about his own destruction.
notes: The bamboo flowers only after a very great length of time (often 60+ years or more), and then dies.

pali: Attanā va kataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā saṅkilissati, attanā akataṁ pāpaṁ, attanā va visujjhati, suddhī asuddhī paccattaṁ, nāñño aññaṁ visodhaye.
english: By oneself alone is a wicked deed done, by oneself is one defiled, by oneself is a wicked deed left undone, by oneself is one purified, purity and impurity come from oneself, (for) no one can purify another.

pali: Atta-d-atthaṁ paratthena bahunā pi na hāpaye; atta-d-attham-abhiññāya sa-d-atthapasuto siyā.
english: One should not neglect one’s own good for another’s, however great; knowing what is good for oneself one should be intent on that good.

pali: Hīnaṁ dhammaṁ na seveyya, pamādena na saṁvase, micchādiṭṭhiṁ na seveyya, na siyā lokavaḍḍhano.
english: One should not follow lowly things, one should not abide heedlessly, one should not follow a wrong view, one should not foster worldliness.
notes: Defined as being the five strands of sense pleasure.

pali: Uttiṭṭhe nappamajjeyya, Dhammaṁ sucaritaṁ care, Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
english: One should strive, not be heedless, one should live by Dhamma, with good conduct, living by Dhamma one lives at ease in this world and the next.

pali: Dhammaṁ care sucaritaṁ, na naṁ duccaritaṁ care, Dhammacārī sukhaṁ seti asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
english: One should live by Dhamma, with good conduct, not with bad conduct, living by Dhamma one lives at ease in this world and the next.

pali: Yathā bubbulakaṁ passe, yathā passe marīcikaṁ, evaṁ lokaṁ avekkhantaṁ Maccurājā na passati.
english: One should see it as a bubble, one should see it as a mirage, looking on the world in this way the King of Death does not see (one).

pali: Etha passathimaṁ lokaṁ cittaṁ rājarathūpamaṁ, yattha bālā visīdanti – natthi saṅgo vijānataṁ.
english: Come, look upon this world adorned like a king’s gilded chariot, where fools become depressed – there is no bond for those who understand.

pali: Yo ca pubbe pamajjitvā, pacchā so nappamajjati, sŏ imaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti abbhā mutto va candimā.
english: Whoever was heedless before, but later is not heedless, that one shines brightly on this world like the moon released from a cloud.

pali: Yassa pāpaṁ kataṁ kammaṁ kusalena pithīyati – sŏ imaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti abbhā mutto va candimā.
english: The one whose wicked deed is covered over by a good deed – that one shines brightly on this world like the moon released from a cloud.

pali: Andhabhūto ayaṁ loko, tanukettha vipassati, sakunto jālamutto va appo saggāya gacchati.
english: This world is blind, few here have true insight, as few go to heaven as birds that escape from the net.

pali: Haṁsādiccapathe yanti, ākāse yanti iddhiyā, nīyanti dhīrā lokamhā, jetvā Māraṁ savāhanaṁ.
english: Geese go through the path of the sky, they go through the firmament by their power, the wise are led out of the world, after beating Māra and his host.

pali: Ekaṁ dhammaṁ atītassa, musāvādissa jantuno, vitiṇṇaparalokassa, natthi pāpaṁ akāriyaṁ.
english: For the person speaking falsely, who has transgressed in this one thing, who has abandoned the next world, there is no wickedness left undone.

pali: Na ve kadariyā devalokaṁ vajanti, bālā have nappasaṁsanti dānaṁ, dhīro ca dānaṁ anumodamāno, teneva so hoti sukhī parattha.
english: The miserly go not to the world of the gods, fools surely do not praise giving, but the wise one rejoices in giving, and through that he is happy hereafter.

pali: Pathavyā ekarajjena, saggassa gamanena vā, sabbalokādhipaccena – sotāpattiphalaṁ varaṁ.
english: Having sole sovereignty over the earth, or going to heaven, or lordship over the whole world – better is the fruit of stream-entry.
notes: These three terms (ekarajjena, gamanena, ādhipaccena) are ablative-like instrumentals.

pali: Yassa jitaṁ nāvajīyati, - jitaṁ assa no yāti koci loke, tam-Buddham-anantagocaraṁ, apadaṁ kena padena nessatha?
english: He whose victory cannot be undone, whose victory no one here approaches, the Buddha, whose range is endless, by what path can you lead the pathless one?

pali: Yassa jālinī visattikā, taṇhā natthi kuhiñci netave, tam-Buddham-anantagocaraṁ, apadaṁ kena padena nessatha?
english: * For him there is no desire, attachment, or craving to lead (him) anywhere, the Buddha, whose range is endless, by what path can you lead the pathless one?
notes: This is the clue to the translation of this verse; what it is talking about is having none of the states (padāni) of craving (taṇhā), etc. by which the one beyond those states (apadaṁ) could be led.

pali: Ye jhānapasutā dhīrā, nekkhammūpasame ratā, devā pi tesaṁ pihayanti, Sambuddhānaṁ satīmataṁ.
english: Those wise ones intent on meditation, who delight in the peace of renunciation, even the gods are envious of them, the Sambuddhas, the ones who are mindful.
notes: Comm: jhānapasutā ti lakkhaṇūpanijjhānaṃ ārammaṇūpanijjhānan-ti; intent on meditation means meditating on the signs, meditating on the (concentration) object.

pali: Kiccho manussapaṭilābho, kicchaṁ maccāna’ jīvitaṁ, kicchaṁ Saddhammasavanaṁ, kiccho Buddhānam-uppādo.
english: It is rare to acquire (birth as a) human, rare is the life of mortals, it is rare to hear the True Dhamma, rare the arising of Buddhas.

pali: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā, sacittapariyodapanaṁ - etaṁ Buddhāna’ sāsanaṁ.
english: The non-doing of anything wicked, undertaking of what is good, the purification of one’s mind - this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

pali: Khantī paramaṁ tapo titikkhā, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ vadanti Buddhā, na hi pabbajito parūpaghātī, samaṇo hoti paraṁ viheṭhayanto.
english: Enduring patience is the supreme austerity, Nibbāna is supreme say the Buddhas, for one gone forth does not hurt another, (nor does) an ascetic harass another.

pali: Anupavādo anupaghāto, pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro, mattaññutā ca bhattasmiṁ, pantañ-ca sayanāsanaṁ, adhicitte ca āyogo - etaṁ Buddhāna’ sāsanaṁ.
english: Not finding fault, not hurting, restraint by the regulations, knowing the right measure of food, (living in) a remote dwelling, devotion to meditation - this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

pali: Na kahāpaṇavassena titti kāmesu vijjati, “Appassādā dukhā kāmā,” iti viññāya paṇḍito,
english: Not through a rain of coins is satisfaction found for sense desires, the wise one knowing: “Sense pleasures have little joy, (much) suffering,”

pali: api dibbesu kāmesu ratiṁ so nādhigacchati. Taṇhakkhayarato hoti Sammāsambuddhasāvako.
english: does not find delight even in heavenly pleasures. The disciple of the Perfect Sambuddha delights in craving’s destruction.

pali: Bahuṁ ve saraṇaṁ yanti pabbatāni vanāni ca ārāmarukkhacetyāni, manussā bhayatajjitā.
english: * Many people shaken by fear go for refuge to woods and mountains, to tree shrines in pleasure parks.

pali: Netaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, netaṁ saraṇam-uttamaṁ, netaṁ saraṇam-āgamma sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
english: That is not a secure refuge, that is not the refuge supreme, that is not the refuge to come to that liberates from all suffering.

pali: Yo ca Buddhañ-ca Dhammañ-ca Saṅghañ-ca saraṇaṁ gato, cattāri ariyasaccāni sammappaññāya passati:
english: Whoever has gone refuge to the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Saṅgha, and who sees with right wisdom the four noble truths:

pali: Dukkhaṁ dukkhasamuppādaṁ dukkhassa ca atikkamaṁ, ariyañ-caṭṭhaṅgikaṁ maggaṁ dukkhūpasamagāminaṁ.
english: Suffering, arising of suffering, and the overcoming of suffering, the eightfold noble path leading to the stilling of suffering.

pali: Etaṁ kho saraṇaṁ khemaṁ, etaṁ saraṇam-uttamaṁ, etaṁ saraṇam-āgamma sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
english: That is a secure refuge, that is the refuge supreme, that is the refuge to come to that liberates from all suffering.

pali: Dullabho purisājañño, na so sabbattha jāyati, yattha so jāyate dhīro, taṁ kulaṁ sukham-edhati.
english: A person of good breed is rare, that one is not born everywhere, wherever that wise one is born, that family gains happiness.

pali: Sukho Buddhānam-uppādo, sukhā Saddhammadesanā, sukhā Saṅghassa sāmaggī, samaggānaṁ tapo sukho.
english: The arising of the Buddhas is good, the teaching of the True Dhamma is good, the harmony of the Saṅgha is good, devotion to harmony is good.

pali: Pūjārahe pūjayato, Buddhe yadi va sāvake, papañcasamatikkante, tiṇṇasokapariddave;
english: For those who worship those worthy of worship, whether Buddhas or disciples, who have overcome the impediments, crossed over grief and lamentation;

pali: te tādise pūjayato, nibbute akutobhaye, na sakkā puññaṁ saṅkhātuṁ, imettam-api kenaci.
english: for those who worship such as these, the emancipated, the fearless, no one is able to measure their (vast) merit, (saying:) it is as much as this.

pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma verinesu averino, verinesu manussesu viharāma averino.
english: Let us live truly happily, without hatred, amongst those who have hatred, amongst humans who have hatred let us live without hatred.

pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma āturesu anāturā, āturesu manussesu viharāma anāturā.
english: Let us live truly happily, without sickness, amongst those who are sick, amongst humans who have sickness let us live without sickness.
notes: Comm: kilesāturesu; amongst those who are sick with defilements.

pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma ussukesu anussukā ussukesu manussesu viharāma anussukā.
english: Let us live truly happily, without longing, amongst those who are longing, amongst humans who are longing let us live without longing.
notes: Comm: pañcakāmaguṇapariyesane; seeking the five strands of sense pleasure.

pali: Susukhaṁ vata jīvāma yesaṁ no natthi kiñcanaṁ, pītibhakkhā bhavissāma devā Ābhassarā yathā.
english: We live truly happily enough having no possessions ourselves, we will feed on joy like the gods of Streaming Light.
notes: Comm: rāgādīsu kiñcanesu; with no possessions like passion and so forth.
The Ābhassara devas are traditionally positioned at the seventeenth level of existence, at the top of the three levels said to correspond to the second absorption.

pali: Jayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, dukkhaṁ seti parājito, upasanto sukhaṁ seti, hitvā jayaparājayaṁ.
english: The victor generates hatred, the defeated one finds suffering, the one at peace lives happily, having abandoned victory and defeat.

pali: Natthi rāgasamo aggi, natthi dosasamo kali, natthi khandhasamā dukkhā, natthi santiparaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: There is no fire like passion, there is no offence like hatred, there is no suffering like the components (of mind and body), no happiness other than peace.
notes: Comm: nibbānato uttariṁ; beyond Nibbāna.

pali: Jighacchā paramā rogā, saṅkhāraparamā dukhā, etaṁ ñatvā yathābhūtaṁ, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: Hunger is the supreme sickness, conditions are the supreme suffering, knowing this as it really is, (know) Nibbāna is the supreme good.

pali: Ārogyaparamā lābhā, santuṭṭhi paramaṁ dhanaṁ, vissāsā paramā ñāti, Nibbānaṁ paramaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: Health is the supreme gain, content the supreme wealth, confidence the supreme kin, Nibbāna the supreme good.

pali: Pavivekarasaṁ pitvā, rasaṁ upasamassa ca, niddaro hoti nippāpo, Dhammapītirasaṁ pivaṁ.
english: Savouring the taste of solitude, and the taste of peace, he is fearless, faultless, savouring the joyful taste of Dhamma.

pali: Sāhu dassanam-ariyānaṁ, sannivāso sadā sukho, adassanena bālānaṁ niccam-eva sukhī siyā.
english: Meeting with the noble is good, living together (with them) is always pleasant, through not meeting foolish people one will constantly be happy.

pali: Bālasaṅgatacārī hi dīgham-addhāna’ socati, dukkho bālehi saṁvāso amitteneva sabbadā, dhīro ca sukhasaṁvāso ñātīnaṁ va samāgamo.
english: For he who consorts with fools grieves for a long time, dwelling with fools is always suffering as it is with enemies, the wise one dwells happily as with an assembly of kin.

pali: tasmā hi, dhīrañ-ca paññañ-ca bahussutañ-ca, dhorayhasīlaṁ vatavantam-ariyaṁ – taṁ tādisaṁ sappurisaṁ sumedhaṁ bhajetha nakkhattapathaṁ va candimā.
english: therefore, the firm, the wise and the learned, the virtuous, dutiful and noble – * (accompany) such a true and intelligent person as the moon accompanies the course of the stars.

pali: Ayoge yuñjam-attānaṁ, yogasmiñ-ca ayojayaṁ, atthaṁ hitvā piyaggāhī, pihetattānuyoginaṁ.
english: Engaging oneself in what is not suitable, not engaging in what is suitable, abandoning the good, grasping the loved, he envies the one who endeavours for himself.

pali: Mā piyehi samāgañchī appiyehi kudācanaṁ, piyānaṁ adassanaṁ dukkhaṁ, appiyānañ-ca dassanaṁ.
english: Do not associate at any time with those who are loved or with those unloved, there is suffering not meeting those loved, and (suffering from) meeting those unloved.

pali: Tasmā piyaṁ na kayirātha, piyāpāyo hi pāpako. Ganthā tesaṁ na vijjanti yesaṁ natthi piyāppiyaṁ.
english: Therefore do not hold (anything) as loved, for losing those who are loved is loathsome. There are no knots for those who hold nothing as loved or as unloved.

pali: Piyato jāyatī soko, piyato jāyatī bhayaṁ, piyato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
english: From love there arises grief, from love there arises fear, for one who is free from love there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali: Pemato jāyatī soko, pemato jāyatī bhayaṁ, pemato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
english: From fondness there arises grief, from fondness there arises fear, for one who is free from fondness there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali: Ratiyā jāyatī soko, ratiyā jāyatī bhayaṁ, ratiyā vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
english: From delight there arises grief, from delight there arises fear, for one who is free from delight there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali: Kāmato jāyatī soko, kāmato jāyatī bhayaṁ, kāmato vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
english: From desire there arises grief, from desire there arises fear, for one who is free from desire there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali: Taṇhāya jāyatī soko, taṇhāya jāyatī bhayaṁ, taṇhāya vippamuttassa natthi soko, kuto bhayaṁ?
english: From craving there arises grief, from craving there arises fear, for one who is free from craving there is no grief, how is there fear?

pali: Sīladassanasampannaṁ, dhammaṭṭhaṁ saccavedinaṁ, attano kamma’ kubbānaṁ, taṁ jano kurute piyaṁ.
english: Endowed with virtue and insight, principled, knowing the truths, doing the deeds that are his own, that one the people love.
notes: Comm: tisso sikkhā tā pūrayamānan-ti attho; the meaning is fulfilling the three trainings (in higher virtue, concentration and wisdom).

pali: Chandajāto anakkhāte, manasā ca phuṭo siyā, kāmesu ca appaṭibaddhacitto, ‘uddhaṁsoto’ ti vuccati.
english: The one with desire arisen for the undeclared, will be suffused with the (awakening) mind, with a mind unconnected with sense pleasures, he is spoken of as ‘one gone upstream’.
notes: I.e. for Nibbāna.
Comm: heṭṭhimehi tīhi maggaphalacittehi phuṭo pūrito bhaveyya; will be filled and suffused with the three lower paths and fruits.

pali: Cirappavāsiṁ purisaṁ dūrato sotthim-āgataṁ, ñātimittā suhajjā ca abhinandanti āgataṁ.
english: When one who lives abroad for a long time comes safely from afar, his relatives, friends and companions come and greatly rejoice.

pali: Tatheva katapuññam-pi asmā lokā paraṁ gataṁ, puññāni paṭigaṇhanti piyaṁ ñātīva āgataṁ.
english: Just so, when one who has performed merit goes from this world unto the next, his merits are received just as relatives come to their loved one.

pali: Kodhaṁ jahe, vippajaheyya mānaṁ, saṁyojanaṁ sabbam-atikkameyya, taṁ nāmarūpasmiṁ asajjamānaṁ, akiñcanaṁ nānupatanti dukkhā.
english: One should abandon anger, one should abandon conceit, one should overcome every fetter, without clinging to mind and bodily form, sufferings never do befall the one having no possessions.
notes: Comm: rāgādīnaṃ abhāvena akiñcanaṁ; not developing possessions like passion and so on.

pali: Yo ve uppatitaṁ kodhaṁ rathaṁ bhantaṁ va dhāraye, tam-ahaṁ sārathiṁ brūmi rasmiggāho itaro jano.
english: Whoever should hold back arisen anger just like a swerving chariot, that one I say is a charioteer, other people are just rein-holders.

pali: Akkodhena jine kodhaṁ, asādhuṁ sādhunā jine, jine kadariyaṁ dānena, saccenālikavādinaṁ.
english: Through kindness one should overcome anger, through goodness one should overcome a lack of goodness, through gifts one should overcome stinginess, through truth (one should overcome) lying speech.
notes: Literally: through non-anger.

pali: Saccaṁ bhaṇe, na kujjheyya, dajjāppasmim-pi yācito, etehi tīhi ṭhānehi gacche devāna’ santike.
english: One should speak out the truth, one should not get angry, when requested give, if only a little, through these three conditions one can go to the presence of the gods.

pali: Ahiṁsakā ye munayo, niccaṁ kāyena saṁvutā, te yanti accutaṁ ṭhānaṁ, yattha gantvā na socare.
english: Those sages without violence, constantly restrained in body, go to the deathless (Nibbāna), having gone there they do not grieve.

pali: Sadā jāgaramānānaṁ, ahorattānusikkhinaṁ, Nibbānaṁ adhimuttānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
english: For those who are always wakeful, who train both by day and by night, who are intent on Nibbāna, the pollutants are laid to rest.

pali: Porāṇam-etaṁ, Atula, netaṁ ajjatanām-iva: nindanti tuṇhim-āsīnaṁ, nindanti bahubhāṇinaṁ, mitabhāṇim-pi nindanti, natthi loke anindito.
english: This is something of old, Atula, this is not something of today: they blame the one who sits silently, they blame the one who talks a lot, they blame the one who talks in moderation, there is no one in the world not blamed.

pali: Na cāhu na ca bhavissati, na cetarahi vijjati ekantaṁ nindito poso, ekantaṁ vā pasaṁsito.
english: There was not and there will not be, and at present there is not found a person totally blameworthy, or one totally praiseworthy.

pali: Yañ-ce viññū pasaṁsanti, anuvicca suve suve, acchiddavuttiṁ medhāviṁ, paññāsīlasamāhitaṁ,
english: The one who, after being examined day by day, is praised by the wise, faultless in conduct, sagacious, attending to virtue and wisdom,

pali: nekkhaṁ jambonadasseva, ko taṁ ninditum-arahati? Devā pi naṁ pasaṁsanti, Brahmunā pi pasaṁsito.
english: one who is like a golden coin, who is there worthy to blame him? That one is praised by the gods, and has been praised by the Brahmās too.

pali: Kāyappakopaṁ rakkheyya, kāyena saṁvuto siyā, kāyaduccaritaṁ hitvā, kāyena sucaritaṁ care.
english: One should guard against bodily anger, one should be restrained bodily, abandoning wrong bodily conduct, one should have good bodily conduct.

pali: Vacīpakopaṁ rakkheyya, vācāya saṁvuto siyā, vacīduccaritaṁ hitvā, vācāya sucaritaṁ care.
english: One should guard against verbal anger, one should be restrained verbally, abandoning wrong verbal conduct, one should have good verbal conduct.

pali: Manopakopaṁ rakkheyya, manasā saṁvuto siyā, manoduccaritaṁ hitvā, manasā sucaritaṁ care.
english: One should guard against mental anger, one should be restrained mentally, abandoning wrong mental conduct, one should have good mental conduct.

pali: Kāyena saṁvutā dhīrā, atho vācāya saṁvutā, manasā saṁvutā dhīrā, te ve suparisaṁvutā.
english: The wise are restrained bodily, then they are restrained verbally, the wise are restrained mentally, they are indeed very well-restrained.

pali: Paṇḍupalāso va dāni ’si, Yamapurisā pi ca taṁ upaṭṭhitā, uyyogamukhe ca tiṭṭhasi, pātheyyam-pi ca te na vijjati.
english: You are now like a withered leaf, Yama’s men stand waiting for you, you stand at decay’s door, with no provisions for the journey found.
notes: Yama is the god of death in traditional Indian lore, his men escort one to the other world.
Comm: kusalapātheyyaṁ; provisions of wholesome deeds.

pali: So karohi dīpam-attano, khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava, niddhantamalo, anaṅgaṇo, dibbaṁ ariyabhūmim-ehisi.
english: One should make an island for oneself, soon the wise one should endeavour, removing the stain, blemishless, you will go to the divine and noble realm.

pali: Upanītavayo ca dāni ’si, sampayāto ’si Yamassa santike, vāso pi ca te natthi antarā, pātheyyam-pi ca te na vijjati.
english: You are now advanced in age, you have come to Yama’s presence, there is nowhere to dwell in between, with no provisions for the journey found.

pali: So karohi dīpam-attano, khippaṁ vāyama paṇḍito bhava, niddhantamalo anaṅgaṇo, na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.
english: One should make an island for oneself, soon the wise one should endeavour, removing the stain, blemishless, you will not come to birth and old age again.

pali: Anupubbena medhāvī, thokathokaṁ khaṇe khaṇe, kammāro rajatasseva, niddhame malam-attano.
english: The sage gradually, little by little, moment by moment, should remove the stain from himself, like a smith (removes the stain) from silver.

pali: Ayasā va malaṁ samuṭṭhitaṁ, taduṭṭhāya tam-eva khādati, evaṁ atidhonacārinaṁ – sakakammāni nayanti duggatiṁ.
english: As a (rust) stain arises from iron, and arisen from that, it eats it away, so with one who is overindulgent – his deeds lead him to a bad destiny.
notes: The commentary says it means being indulgent in regard to the four requisites.

pali: Asajjhāyamalā mantā, anuṭṭhānamalā gharā, malaṁ vaṇṇassa kosajjaṁ, pamādo rakkhato malaṁ.
english: Lack of repetition is the ruin of chants, a lack of maintenance is the ruin of homes, indolence is the ruin of one’s appearance, heedlessness is the ruin of the one on guard.
notes: Mala, the same word is translated as stain elsewhere, but here the only translation I feel that works throughout the verse is ruin.

pali: Malitthiyā duccaritaṁ, maccheraṁ dadato malaṁ, malā ve pāpakā dhammā asmiṁ loke paramhi ca.
english: Bad conduct is a woman’s stain, stinginess is a giver’s stain, wicked actions are indeed stains both in this world and in the next.

pali: Tato malā malataraṁ, avijjā paramaṁ malaṁ, etaṁ malaṁ pahatvāna, nimmalā hotha, bhikkhavo!
english: A stain that is worse than that stain, ignorance is the supreme stain, after abandoning that stain, be without stains, O monastics!
notes: Note that this is the last mention of stains (mala) in this chapter, although related themes make up the rest of the chapter.

pali: Sujīvaṁ ahirikena, kākasūrena dhaṁsinā, pakkhandinā pagabbhena, saṅkiliṭṭhena jīvitaṁ.
english: Life is light for one without shame, with the bold courage of a crow, living a life with backbiting, recklessness, and defilements.

pali: Hirīmatā ca dujjīvaṁ, niccaṁ sucigavesinā, alīnenāpagabbhena, suddhājīvena passatā.
english: Life is hard when endowed with shame, for the one constantly seeking purity, for one sincere, and not reckless, looking for purity of life.

pali: Yo pāṇam-atipāteti, musāvādañ-ca bhāsati, loke adinnaṁ ādiyati, paradārañ-ca gacchati,
english: Whoever kills a living being, and speaks a word that is not true, takes what is not given here, and goes to another’s wife,

pali: surāmerayapānañ-ca yo naro anuyuñjati, idhevam-eso lokasmiṁ mūlaṁ khaṇati attano.
english: that person who is devoted to a drink of liquor and wine, digs up his own root right here in the world.
