pali: Evaṁ bho purisa jānāhi, pāpadhammā asaññatā, mā taṁ lobho adhammo ca ciraṁ dukkhāya randhayuṁ.
english: Know it thus, dear sir, a lack of restraint is a bad thing, let not greed and corruption oppress you with suffering for a long time.

pali: Dadāti ve yathāsaddhaṁ, yathāpasādanaṁ jano, tattha yo maṅku bhavati paresaṁ pānabhojane na so divā vā rattiṁ vā, samādhiṁ adhigacchati.
english: The people give according to faith, according to their confidence, herein the one who becomes dejected because of food and drink (given) to others he does not, either by day or nigh attain to (good) concentration.
notes: Meaning, broadly, others’ gains.

pali: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ, mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ, sa ve divā vā rattiṁ vā, samādhiṁ adhigacchati.
english: For the one in whom this (dejection) is cut off, destroyed at the root, dug up, does, by day and night, attain to (good) concentration.

pali: Natthi rāgasamo aggi, natthi dosasamo gaho, natthi mohasamaṁ jālaṁ, natthi taṇhāsamā nadī.
english: There is no fire that is like passion, there is nothing that takes a hold like hatred, there is no snare like delusion, there is no flood like craving.

pali: Sudassaṁ vajjam-aññesaṁ, attano pana duddasaṁ, paresaṁ hi so vajjāni opuṇāti yathā bhusaṁ, attano pana chādeti, kaliṁ va kitavā saṭho.
english: Easy to see are others’ fault, but one’s own is hard to see, for one sifts other people’s faults like they were chaff, but conceals one’s own (faults), like a crafty cheat (conceals) his defeat.
notes: The commentary explains this last line differently, saying that saṭha means a hunter who conceals his body (kali) in order to catch his prey. I know of nowhere else that saṭha means a hunter, or kali means a body; if it were correct then we could translate: like a hunter (conceals) his body.

pali: Paravajjānupassissa niccaṁ ujjhānasaññino, āsavā tassa vaḍḍhanti, ārā so āsavakkhayā.
english: The one who constantly looks for another’s fault, who is an abject complainer, for him the pollutants increase, he is far from their destruction.

pali: Ākāse va padaṁ natthi, samaṇo natthi bāhire, papañcābhiratā pajā, nippapañcā Tathāgatā.
english: There is no footprint in the sky, there is no ascetic on the outside, folk greatly delight in impediments, the Realised Ones are free of impediments.

pali: Ākāse va padaṁ natthi, samaṇo natthi bāhire, saṅkhārā sassatā natthi, natthi Buddhānam-iñjitaṁ.
english: There is no footprint in the sky, there is no ascetic on the outside, there are no constant conditions, there is no disturbance for the Buddhas.

pali: Na tena hoti Dhammaṭṭho yenatthaṁ sahasā naye, yo ca atthaṁ anatthañ-ca ubho niccheyya paṇḍito.
english: One who would hastily settle a case because of that is not one who stands by Dhamma, the wise one should discriminate the two: what is the case and what is not the case.

pali: Asāhasena dhammena samena nayatī pare, Dhammassa gutto medhāvī, Dhammaṭṭho ti pavuccati.
english: The one who settles for other people without haste, justly and impartially, the sagacious one, protecting Dhamma, is said to be one who stands by Dhamma.
notes: This is the last mention of dhammaṭṭha in this chapter.

pali: Na tena paṇḍito hoti yāvatā bahu bhāsati; khemī averī abhayo, paṇḍito ti pavuccati.
english: One is not a wise person merely because of speaking much; being safe, hatred-free, fearless, one is called a wise person.

pali: Na tāvatā Dhammadharo yāvatā bahu bhāsati, yo ca appam-pi sutvāna, Dhammaṁ kāyena passati, sa ve Dhammadharo hoti, yo Dhammaṁ nappamajjati.
english: One is not a Dhamma-bearer merely through speaking much, but the one who, having heard a little, sees Dhamma for himself, is one who bears Dhamma, the one who is not heedless regarding Dhamma.
notes: Literally: with the body, but for himself, perhaps as an analogue of attanā, seems to be the meaning.

pali: Na tena thero hoti yenassa palitaṁ siro, paripakko vayo tassa moghajiṇṇo ti vuccati.
english: One is not an elder because one’s head has grey hair, for the one who is (only) well-matured, aged, is said to be old in vain.

pali: Yamhi saccañ-ca Dhammo ca ahiṁsā saṁyamo damo, sa ve vantamalo dhīro thero iti pavuccati.
english: In whom is truth, Dhamma, non-violence, restraint and (good) training, the wise one who throws out the stain is (truly) called an elder.

pali: Na vākkaraṇamattena vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā sādhurūpo naro hoti, issukī maccharī saṭho;
english: Not by eloquence only, or by a beautiful complexion, is a person honourable, (if still) jealous, selfish and deceitful;

pali: yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ, mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ, sa vantadoso medhāvī sādhurūpo ti vuccati.
english: for the one in whom this is cut off, destroyed at the root, dug up, that sage who has thrown out hatred is said to be honourable.

pali: Na muṇḍakena samaṇo, abbato alikaṁ bhaṇaṁ, icchālobhasamāpanno, samaṇo kiṁ bhavissati?
english: Not through a shaven head is one an ascetic, (if) one lacks vows, speaks lies, and is endowed with greed and desire, how will one be an ascetic?
notes: Comm: sīlavatena ca dhūtavatena ca virahito; being without the vow of virtue and the vow of asceticism.

pali: Yo ca sameti pāpāni, aṇuṁ-thūlāni sabbaso – samitattā hi pāpānaṁ samaṇo ti pavuccati.
english: The one who pacifies wicked deeds, small and great, in every way – through the pacifing of wicked deeds he is said to be an ascetic.

pali: Na tena bhikkhu hoti yāvatā bhikkhate pare, vissaṁ Dhammaṁ samādāya bhikkhu hoti na tāvatā.
english: One is not a monastic merely through eating others’ almsfood, the one who undertakes a false Dhamma to that extent is not a monastic.

pali: Yodha puññañ-ca pāpañ-ca bāhetvā brahmacariyavā, saṅkhāya loke carati sa ce, bhikkhū ti vuccati.
english: * If he is one who lives the holy life here, warding off both merit and demerit, and wanders with discrimination in the world, that one is said to be a monastic.

pali: Na monena munī hoti mūḷharūpo aviddasu, yo ca tulaṁ va paggayha, varam-ādāya paṇḍito.
english: Not through silence is a deluded fool (considered to be) a seer, the wise one, like one holding the balance, takes up what is noble.

pali: Pāpāni parivajjeti sa munī tena so muni, yo munāti ubho loke muni tena pavuccati.
english: The seer who rejects wicked deeds through that is (considered) a seer, whoever understands both worlds because of that is said to be a seer.

pali: Na tena ariyo hoti yena pāṇāni hiṁsati, ahiṁsā sabbapāṇānaṁ ariyo ti pavuccati.
english: Not through hurting breathing beings one is noble, the one who does not hurt any breathing beings is said to be noble.

pali: Na sīlabbatamattena, bāhusaccena vā pana, atha vā samādhilābhena, vivittasayanena vā,
english: Not merely through virtue or vows, or through great learning, or through the attainment of concentration, or through a secluded dwelling,

pali: phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṁ, aputhujjanasevitaṁ; bhikkhu vissāsa’ māpādi appatto āsavakkhayaṁ.
english: do I attain the happiness of renunciation, not practised by worldly people; let a monastic not be confident (as long as) the destruction of the pollutants is unattained.
notes: Defined by the commentary as anāgāmisukhaṁ; the happiness of non-returning.
This parses as vissāsaṁ mā āpādi.
There is an uncertainty of person in this verse (I and then he), it might have been better written with 3rd person phusatī (with long -ī for the metre): does he attain...

pali: Maggānaṭṭhaṅgiko seṭṭho, saccānaṁ caturo padā, virāgo seṭṭho dhammānaṁ, dipadānañ-ca Cakkhumā.
english: The eightfold is the best of paths, four principles (the best) of truths, passionlessness the best of states, the Visionary (the best) of men.
notes: Lit: of bipeds.

pali: Eso va maggo natthañño, dassanassa visuddhiyā, etaṁ hi tumhe paṭipajjatha, Mārassetaṁ pamohanaṁ.
english: This is the path, there is no other, for insight and for purity, you should enter upon this path, this is the confounding of Māra.

pali: Etaṁ hi tumhe paṭipannā dukkhassantaṁ karissatha, akkhāto ve mayā maggo, aññāya sallasanthanaṁ.
english: Having entered upon this path you will make an end to suffering, the path was declared by me, the removal of the dart by knowledge.

pali: Tumhehi kiccaṁ ātappaṁ akkhātāro Tathāgatā, paṭipannā pamokkhanti jhāyino Mārabandhanā.
english: Your duty is to have ardour declare the Realised Ones, entering this path meditators will be released from the bonds of Māra.

pali: Sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
english: All conditions are impermanent, when one sees this with wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering – this is the path to purity.

pali: Sabbe saṅkhārā dukkhā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
english: All conditions are suffering, when one sees this with wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering – this is the path to purity.

pali: Sabbe dhammā anattā ti, yadā paññāya passati, atha nibbindatī dukkhe – esa maggo visuddhiyā.
english: All components (of mind and body) are without self, when one sees this with wisdom, then one grows tired of suffering – this is the path to purity.

pali: Uṭṭhānakālamhi anuṭṭhahāno, yuvā balī, ālasiyaṁ upeto, saṁsannasaṅkappamano kusīto – paññāya maggaṁ alaso na vindati.
english: The one who has not energy at a time for energy, youthful, strong, (but) given to laziness, whose mind lacks (right) intention and is indolent – the lazy one does not find wisdom’s path.

pali: Vācānurakkhī manasā susaṁvuto, kāyena ca akusalaṁ na kayirā, ete tayo kammapathe visodhaye, ārādhaye maggaṁ isippaveditaṁ.
english: Verbally guarded, well-restrained in mind, not doing a wrong deed with the body, one should purify these three paths of action, one should undertake the path shown by seers.

pali: Yogā ve jāyatī bhūri, ayogā bhūrisaṅkhayo, etaṁ dvedhāpathaṁ ñatvā bhavāya vibhavāya ca, tathattānaṁ niveseyya yathā bhūri pavaḍḍhati.
english: From effort arises wisdom, without effort wisdom is destroyed, having understood these two paths of development and decline, one should establish oneself so that one’s wisdom increases.

pali: Vanaṁ chindatha mā rukkhaṁ, vanato jāyatī bhayaṁ, chetvā vanañ-ca vanathañ-ca, nibbanā hotha bhikkhavo.
english: Cut down the forest (of defilements) not just a tree, from the forest arises a danger, having cut down the forest and thicket, you should be without forests, monastics.
notes: Comm: rāgādikilesavanaṁ.

pali: Yāva hi vanatho na chijjati aṇumatto pi narassa nārisu, paṭibaddhamano va tāva so, vaccho khīrapako va mātari.
english: * For as long as an atom of desire of a man for a woman is not cut down, for just so long is the mind in bondage, like a calf (in bondage) to mother’s milk.
notes: This is a play on the word vanatha, which also occurs in the previous verse, and means both a thicket and in metaphorical usage the thicket of desire.

pali: Ucchinda sineham-attano, kumudaṁ sāradikaṁ va pāṇinā, santimaggam-eva brūhaya Nibbānaṁ Sugatena desitaṁ.
english: Cut off (any) affection for one’s self, like an autumn lotus (plucked) with the hand, develop fully the path to peace and Nibbāna taught by the Happy One.

pali: “Idha vassaṁ vasissāmi, idha hemantagimhisu”, iti bālo vicinteti, antarāyaṁ na bujjhati.
english: “Here I will dwell during the rains, here during winter and summer”, in just such a way a fool thinks, not understanding the danger.

pali: Taṁ puttapasusammattaṁ byāsattamanasaṁ naraṁ, suttaṁ gāmaṁ mahogho va maccu ādāya gacchati.
english: That person whose mind is attached and besotted by cattle and children, is snatched away by death just as a sleeping village (by) a great flood.
notes: As we really need an instrumental here, it might have been better to write: suttaṁ gāmaṁ ogheneva.

pali: Na santi puttā tāṇāya, na pitā na pi bandhavā, Antakenādhipannassa natthi ñātisu tāṇatā.
english: Children are not a refuge, nor fathers, not even kin, for one overcome by the End-Maker there is no refuge in relatives.
notes: I.e. Māra incarnate, or death.

pali: Etam-atthavasaṁ ñatvā, paṇḍito sīlasaṁvuto, Nibbānagamanaṁ maggaṁ khippam-eva visodhaye.
english: Understanding the truth of this the wise one, endowed with virtue, should quickly purify the path that is leading to Nibbāna.

pali: Mattāsukhapariccāgā, passe ce vipulaṁ sukhaṁ, caje mattāsukhaṁ dhīro, sampassaṁ vipulaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: If, by renouncing a small good, he might see a good that is large, the wise one should renounce that small good, seeing the good that is extensive.

pali: Paradukkhūpadānena attano sukham-icchati, verasaṁsaggasaṁsaṭṭho, verā so na parimuccati.
english: One who desires happiness for oneself by causing suffering for another, being associated thus with hatred, is not fully released from that hatred.

pali: Yaṁ hi kiccaṁ tad-apaviddhaṁ, akiccaṁ pana kayirati, unnalānaṁ pamattānaṁ, tesaṁ vaḍḍhanti āsavā.
english: That to be done is rejected, but what is not to be done is done, for the insolent, the heedless, their pollutants increase.

pali: Yesañ-ca susamāraddhā niccaṁ kāyagatā sati akiccaṁ te na sevanti, kicce sātaccakārino, satānaṁ sampajānānaṁ, atthaṁ gacchanti āsavā.
english: But for those who always properly undertake mindfulness of the body who do not practice what is not to be done, persisting in what is to be done, for those mindful ones, those fully aware, the pollutants are laid to rest.

pali: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā, rājāno dve ca khattiye, raṭṭhaṁ sānucaraṁ hantvā, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.
english: Destroying mother and father, and (then) two noble kings, destroying a kingdom and its followers, the brahmin proceeds untroubled.
notes: The commentary interprets this verse to mean: destroying craving and the conceit ‘I am’, and the two: eternalism and annihilationism, destroying passionate delight in the twelve sense spheres, the one without pollutants proceeds untroubled.

pali: Mātaraṁ pitaraṁ hantvā, rājāno dve ca sotthiye, veyyagghapañcamaṁ hantvā, anīgho yāti brāhmaṇo.
english: Destroying mother and father, and two prosperous kings, destroying a tiger as the fifth, the brahmin proceeds untroubled.
notes: This is often interpreted as being equal to sottiye, learned; but there is no reason why we can’t translate it according to how it is written as sotthiye, prosperous, blessed. The commentary says two prosperous kings here means two brahmin kings.

The commentary interprets this verse to mean: destroying craving and the conceit ‘I am’, and the two: eternalism and annihilationism, destroying the five hindrances having doubt as the fifth, the one without pollutants proceeds untroubled.

pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ Buddhagatā sati.
english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Buddha.

pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ Dhammagatā sati.
english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Dhamma.

pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ Saṅghagatā sati.
english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the Saṅgha.

pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca niccaṁ kāyagatā sati.
english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night constantly have mindfulness of the body.

pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā, yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca ahiṁsāya rato mano.
english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night have a mind that delights in non-violence.

pali: Suppabuddhaṁ pabujjhanti sadā Gotamasāvakā yesaṁ divā ca ratto ca bhāvanāya rato mano.
english: Gotama’s disciples always awake to a good wakening, those who day and night have a mind that delights in cultivation.

pali: Duppabbajjaṁ durabhiramaṁ, durāvāsā gharā dukhā, dukkhosamānasaṁvāso, dukkhānupatitaddhagū, tasmā na caddhagū siyā, na ca dukkhānupatito siyā.
english: The going forth is hard, it is hard to find delight (therein), (but) it is (also) hard to dwell in households that are suffering, dwelling together with those different is suffering, travellers (in the round of births) are affected by suffering, therefore do not be a traveller, do not be affected by suffering.

pali: Saddho sīlena sampanno yasobhogasamappito, yaṁ yaṁ padesaṁ bhajati, tattha tattheva pūjito.
english: The faithful one who is endowed with virtue, and has wealth and fame, whatever district he resorts to, right there and then he is worshipped.

pali: Dūre santo pakāsenti, himavanto va pabbato, asantettha na dissanti, rattiṁ khittā yathā sarā.
english: The good are visible from far, like a mountain covered in snow, (but) the wicked are not seen here, just like arrows shot in the night.
notes: The commentary says visible means coming within the range of knowledge of the Buddhas; and the wicked are those who have set their sight on material rewards.

pali: Ekāsanaṁ ekaseyyaṁ, eko caram-atandito, eko damayam-attānaṁ vanante ramito siyā.
english: Sitting alone, lying down alone, walking alone, diligent, the solitary one who trains himself will delight in the edge of a forest.

pali: Abhūtavādī nirayaṁ upeti, yo vāpi katvā ‘Na karomī’ ti cāha, ubho pi te pecca samā bhavanti nihīnakammā manujā parattha.
english: The one who speaks falsely goes to the underworld, and he who says: ‘I did not do’ what he has done, both of these are just the same when they have gone to the hereafter, (they are) humans who did base deeds.

pali: Kāsāvakaṇṭhā bahavo pāpadhammā asaññatā, pāpā pāpehi kammehi nirayaṁ te upapajjare.
english: Many wearing the monastic robe around their necks are wicked, unrestrained, the wicked through their wicked deeds re-arisein the underworld.

pali: Seyyo ayoguḷo bhutto tatto, aggisikhūpamo, yañ-ce bhuñjeyya dussīlo raṭṭhapiṇḍaṁ asaññato.
english: It’s better to have eaten a glowing iron ball, like a flame of fire, than that (the monastic) who is unrestrained and unvirtuous should enjoy the country’s almsfood.

pali: Cattāri ṭhānāni naro pamatto, āpajjatī paradārūpasevī: apuññalābhaṁ, nanikāmaseyyaṁ, nindaṁ tatīyaṁ, nirayaṁ catutthaṁ.
english: There are four states the man who is heedless, the man who consorts with other man’s wives, undergoes: he gains demerit, an uncomfortable bed, blame as third, and (rebirth in) the underworld as fourth.

pali: Apuññalābho ca gatī ca pāpikā, bhītassa bhītāya ratī ca thokikā, rājā ca daṇḍaṁ garukaṁ paṇeti, tasmā naro paradāraṁ na seve.
english: Gaining demerit and a bad destiny, and (only) the small delight of a scared man with a scared woman, and kings who apply heavy punishment, a man therefore should not consort with another’s wife.

pali: Kuso yathā duggahito hattham-evānukantati, sāmaññaṁ dupparāmaṭṭhaṁ nirayāyupakaḍḍhati.
english: As jagged grass, wrongly grasped, cuts into the hand, so does the ascetic life, wrongly grasped, drag one down to the underworld.
notes: Kusa is a particular type of grass, see Nature s.v. Kusa: A type of perennial grass with a sharp spiky leaf growing up to 0.9 m. high and with deep roots; but the commentary here defines it to mean any grass that is capable of cutting, including palm leaves, hence the translation.

pali: Yaṁ kiñci sithilaṁ kammaṁ saṅkiliṭṭhañ-ca yaṁ vataṁ, saṅkassaraṁ brahmacariyaṁ na taṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english: Whatever lax deed there is and that vow which is defiled, (know that) a holy life that is doubtful does not have great fruit for that one.

pali: Kayirañ-ce kayirāthenaṁ, daḷham-enaṁ parakkame, saṭhilo hi paribbājo bhiyyo ākirate rajaṁ.
english: If he would do what should be done, he should be firm in his effort, for the wanderer who is lax spreads a lot of impurity.

pali: Akataṁ dukkataṁ seyyo, pacchā tapati dukkataṁ, katañ-ca sukataṁ seyyo, yaṁ katvā nānutappati.
english: Better undone is a wrong-doing, a wrong-doing one later regrets, better done is what is well-done, which, when done, one does not regret.

pali: Nagaraṁ yathā paccantaṁ guttaṁ santarabāhiraṁ, evaṁ gopetha attānaṁ, khaṇo vo mā upaccagā, khaṇātītā hi socanti nirayamhi samappitā.
english: As a border town is guarded on the inside and the outside, so one should watch over oneself, and you should not let the moment pass, for when the chance has passed they grieve when consigned to the underworld.

pali: Alajjitāye lajjanti, lajjitāye na lajjare, micchādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
english: They are ashamed of what is not shameful, not ashamed of what is shameful, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny.

pali: Abhaye bhayadassino, bhaye cābhayadassino, micchādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
english: Seeing fear in what is not fearful, not seeing fear in what is fearful, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny.

pali: Avajje vajjamatino, vajje cāvajjadassino, micchādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti duggatiṁ.
english: Finding blame in what is blameless, not seeing blame in what is blameable, undertaking wrong views, beings go to a bad destiny.

pali: Vajjañ-ca vajjato ñatvā, avajjañ-ca avajjato, sammādiṭṭhisamādānā sattā gacchanti suggatiṁ.
english: Knowing blame in what is blameable, and no blame in what is blameless, undertaking right views, beings go to a good destiny.

pali: Ahaṁ nāgo va saṅgāme cāpāto patitaṁ saraṁ ativākyaṁ titikkhissaṁ, dussīlo hi bahujjano.
english: Like an elephant in battle (endures) an arrow shot from bow (so) will I endure abuse, for many people are unvirtuous.

pali: Dantaṁ nayanti samitiṁ, dantaṁ rājābhirūhati, danto seṭṭho manussesu, yotivākyaṁ titikkhati.
english: They lead one trained into a crowd, a king mounts one who has been trained, amongst humans one trained is best, the one who can endure abuse.

pali: Varam-assatarā dantā, ājānīyā ca Sindhavā, kuñjarā ca mahānāgā, attadanto tato varaṁ.
english: Noble are the well-trained horses, the well-bred horses from Sindh, and the great tusker elephants, (and even) more noble than that is the one who has trained himself.

pali: Na hi etehi yānehi gaccheyya agataṁ disaṁ, yathattanā sudantena, danto dantena gacchati.
english: Not by these vehicles can one go to the place beyond destinations, as one through training himself well, being trained by the training, goes.

pali: Dhanapālakŏ nāma kuñjaro kaṭukappabhedano dunnivārayo, baddho kabalaṁ na bhuñjati, sumarati nāgavanassa kuñjaro.
english: The tusker named Dhanapālaka musty in rut, difficult to restrain, bound, he doesn’t eat (even) a morsel, the tusker remembers the elephant forest.
notes: The verse is unusual in that it has no moral outside of the story which is attached to it.

pali: Middhī yadā hoti mahagghaso ca, niddāyitā samparivattasāyī, mahāvarāho va nivāpapuṭṭho, punappunaṁ gabbham-upeti mando.
english: When one is torpid and overeats, sleepy and rolling on the bed, like a great pig fed on fodder, that fool comes to the womb again.

pali: Idaṁ pure cittam-acāri cārikaṁ yenicchakaṁ yatthakāmaṁ yathāsukhaṁ, tad-ajjahaṁ niggahessāmi yoniso, hatthim-pabhinnaṁ viya aṅkusaggaho.
english: Formerly this wandering mind wandered through desire, pleasure and happiness, (but) today I will control it wisely, like one with goad an elephant in rut.

pali: Appamādavaggo Dutiyo Related Verse from the Dhammapada Appamādaratā hotha, sacittam-anurakkhatha, duggā uddharathattānaṁ paṅke sanno va kuñjaro.
english: The Chapter about Heedfulness, the Second You should delight in heedfulness, you should always protect your mind, you should raise yourself from this pit like the tusker sunk in the mud.

pali: Sace labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ saddhiṁcaraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ, abhibhuyya sabbāni parissayāni careyya tenattamano satīmā.
english: If you should find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, overcoming all your troubles you should live with that one, glad and mindful.

pali: No ce labhetha nipakaṁ sahāyaṁ saddhiṁcaraṁ sādhuvihāridhīraṁ, rājā va raṭṭhaṁ vijitaṁ pahāya eko care mātaṅgaraññe va nāgo.
english: If you do not find a prudent friend or companion, one who lives well, a wise one, like a king who abandons his conquered kingdom one should live alone like a solitary elephant in the forest.

pali: Ekassa caritaṁ seyyo, natthi bāle sahāyatā, eko care na ca pāpāni kayirā, appossukko mātaṅgaraññe va nāgo.
english: It is better to live alone, there can be no friendship with a fool, one should live alone and not do anything bad, unconcerned like a solitary elephant in the forest.

pali: Atthamhi jātamhi sukhā sahāyā, tuṭṭhī sukhā yā itarītarena, puññaṁ sukhaṁ jīvitasaṅkhayamhi, sabbassa dukkhassa sukhaṁ pahāṇaṁ.
english: Friends are good whenever need arises, being content with everything is good, at the break-up of life merit is good, the abandoning of all suffering is good.

pali: Sukhā matteyyatā loke, atho petteyyatā sukhā, sukhā sāmaññatā loke, atho brahmaññatā sukhā.
english: Respecting one’s mother is good in the world, also respecting one’s father is good, respecting ascetics is good in the world, also respecting (true) brahmins is good.

pali: Sukhaṁ yāva jarā sīlaṁ, sukhā saddhā patiṭṭhitā, sukho paññāya paṭilābho, pāpānaṁ akaraṇaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: Virtuous conduct till old age is good, the establishing of faith is good, the acquisition of wisdom is good, doing nothing wicked is good.

pali: Manujassa pamattacārino taṇhā vaḍḍhati māluvā viya, so palavatī hurāhuraṁ phalam-icchaṁ va vanasmi’ vānaro.
english: For a human who lives life heedlessly craving increases like a clinging creeper, he rushes from one place to another like a monkey desiring fruit in the forest.

pali: Yaṁ esā sahatī jammī taṇhā loke visattikā, sokā tassa pavaḍḍhanti abhivaṭṭhaṁ va bīraṇaṁ.
english: That one who is overcome by these low cravings and attachments in the world, for him griefs increase like grass that has had heavy rain.

pali: Yo cetaṁ sahatī jammiṁ taṇhaṁ loke duraccayaṁ, sokā tamhā papatanti udabindu va pokkharā.
english: Whoever overcomes this low craving in the world, which is difficult to get past, griefs fall from him like a drop of water from a lotus.

pali: Taṁ vo vadāmi: “Bhaddaṁ vo yāvantettha samāgatā”, taṇhāya mūlaṁ khaṇatha, usīrattho va bīraṇaṁ, mā vo naḷaṁ va soto va Māro bhañji punappunaṁ.
english: This I say to you: “Good luck to as many as have assembled here”, dig up the root of craving, like one seeking the root (digs up) grass, do not let Māra push you down again like a stream (pushes down) the reed.
notes: The commentary paraphrases with: usīrena atthiko.

pali: Yathā pi mūle anupaddave daḷhe chinno pi rukkho, punar-eva rūhati, evam-pi taṇhānusaye anūhate nibbattatī dukkham-idaṁ punappunaṁ.
english: Just as when the root remains firm and untroubled though the tree was cut down, it grows again, so when the tendency to craving is not rooted out this suffering appears again and again.
notes: A locative absolutive construction.

pali: Yassa chattiṁsatī sotā manāpassavanā bhusā, vāhā vahanti duddiṭṭhiṁ saṅkappā rāganissitā.
english: He in whom the thirty-six streams flow pleasantly and strong, the one with wrong view, is carried away by his passionate intentions.
notes: The number is arrived at by multiplying the types of craving (for pleasure, continuity and discontinuity) by the six internal and external sense spheres.

pali: Savanti sabbadhī sotā, latā ubbhijja tiṭṭhati, tañ-ca disvā lataṁ jātaṁ mūlaṁ paññāya chindatha.
english: Streams are flowing everywhere, the creepers remain where they grow, seeing this, cut the creeper’s root that has arisen with wisdom.

pali: Saritāni sinehitāni ca sŏmanassāni bhavanti jantuno, te sātasitā sukhesino, te ve jātijarūpagā narā.
english: * There are flowing streams of affection and mental happinesses for a person, pleasure-dependent they seek happiness, those people undergo both birth and old age.

pali: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā parisappanti saso va bādhito, saṁyojanasaṅgasattakā dukkham-upenti punappunaṁ cirāya.
english: People surrounded by craving crawl round like a hare in a trap, attached and clinging to fetters they come back again and again to suffering for a long time.
notes: Often translated as runs around, but a hare in a trap isn’t running anywhere. Commentary paraphrases with saṁsappanti.

pali: Tasiṇāya purakkhatā pajā parisappanti saso va bādhito, tasmā tasiṇaṁ vinodaye – bhikkhu ākaṅkha’ virāgam-attano.
english: People surrounded by craving crawl round like a hare in a trap, therefore he should remove craving – the monk who longs for dispassion for himself.

pali: Yo nibbanatho vanādhimutto, vanamutto vanam-eva dhāvati, taṁ puggalam-etha passatha, mutto bandhanam-eva dhāvati.
english: The one who is free from desires, who is intent on the forest, (though) free from the forest, runs back to the forest, come here and look at that person, (though) free, he runs back to bondage.
notes: It is hard to get the meaning across without greatly expanding the translation, the forest is the forest of desires.

pali: Na taṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanam-āhu dhīrā, yad-āyasaṁ dārujaṁ pabbajañ-ca, sārattarattā maṇikuṇḍalesu puttesu dāresu ca yā apekhā –
english: That bondage is not so strong say the wise, that is made of iron or wood or reeds, * impassioned and excited they seek out jewels and earrings and children and wives –

pali: etaṁ daḷhaṁ bandhanam-āhu dhīrā, ohārinaṁ sithilaṁ, duppamuñcaṁ, etam-pi chetvāna paribbajanti anapekkhino, kāmasukhaṁ pahāya.
english: that bondage is strong say the wise, dragging down the lax, hard to get free from, having cut this down they wander about seeking nothing, abandoning the happiness in pleasure.

pali: Ye rāgarattānupatanti sotaṁ sayaṁkataṁ makkaṭako va jālaṁ, etam-pi chetvāna vajanti dhīrā, anapekkhino sabbadukkhaṁ pahāya.
english: Those who are impassioned by passion follow the stream like a spider a web made by itself, having cut this away the wise proceed, seeking nothing, abandoning all suffering.

pali: Muñca pure, muñca pacchato, majjhe muñca, bhavassa pāragū, sabbattha vimuttamānaso, na punaṁ jātijaraṁ upehisi.
english: Be free of the past, be free of the future, be free of the present, after crossing over (all) existence, with mind liberated in every way, you will not return to birth and old age.

pali: Vitakkapamathitassa jantuno tibbarāgassa, subhānupassino, bhiyyo taṇhā pavaḍḍhati, esa kho daḷhaṁ karoti bandhanaṁ.
english: For a person crushed by thoughts and pierced by passion, contemplating the attractive, craving increases much more, this surely makes the bond more firm.

pali: Vitakkupasame ca yo rato asubhaṁ bhāvayatī sadā sato, esa kho vyantikāhiti, esacchecchati Mārabandhanaṁ.
english: Whoever has delight in the calming of thoughts, who always mindfully cultivates what is unattractive, will surely abolish this (craving), he will cut off the bond of Māra.

pali: Niṭṭhaṁ gato asantāsī, vītataṇho anaṅgaṇo, acchindi bhavasallāni, antimoyaṁ samussayo.
english: Having gone to the end, without trembling, without craving, without impurity, cutting off the darts of existence, this one is his final body.

pali: Vītataṇho anādāno, niruttipadakovido, akkharānaṁ sannipātaṁ jaññā pubbaparāni ca, sa ve antimasārīro mahāpañño (mahāpuriso) ti vuccati.
english: Without craving, without attachment, skilled in words and their explanation, knowing how syllables are arranged, which come before and which after, the one in his final body is said to be (a great person), one of great wisdom.

pali: Sabbābhibhū sabbavidūham-asmi, sabbesu dhammesu anūpalitto, sabbañjaho taṇhakkhaye vimutto, sayaṁ abhiññāya, kam-uddiseyyaṁ.
english: All-Conquering, All-Wise am I, undefiled regarding all things, having given up everything, liberated through craving’s destruction, when having deep knowledge myself, who should I point to (as Teacher)?

pali: Sabbadānaṁ Dhammadānaṁ jināti, sabbaṁ rasaṁ Dhammaraso jināti, sabbaṁ ratiṁ Dhammaratiṁ jināti, taṇhakkhayo sabbadukkhaṁ jināti.
english: The gift of the Dhamma surpasses all other gifts, the taste of the Dhamma surpasses all other tastes, the love of the Dhamma surpasses all other loves, destruction of craving overcomes all suffering.

pali: Hananti bhogā dummedhaṁ no ve pāragavesino, bhogataṇhāya dummedho hanti aññe va attanaṁ.
english: Riches destroy the stupid one who does not seek the way beyond, through his craving for riches the stupid one destroys others and himself.

pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, rāgadosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vītarāgesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by passion, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without passion.

pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, dosadosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vītadosesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by hatred, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without hatred.

pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, mohadosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vītamohesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by delusion, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without delusion.

pali: Tiṇadosāni khettāni, icchādosā ayaṁ pajā, tasmā hi vigaticchesu dinnaṁ hoti mahapphalaṁ.
english: Fields are ruined by grassy weeds, these people are ruined by desire, therefore there is great fruit for that given to those without desire.

pali: Cakkhunā saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu sotena saṁvaro, ghāṇena saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu jivhāya saṁvaro,
english: Restraint of eye is good, restraint of ear is good, restraint of nose is good, restraint of tongue is good,

pali: kāyena saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu vācāya saṁvaro, manasā saṁvaro sādhu, sādhu sabbattha saṁvaro, sabbattha saṁvuto bhikkhu sabbadukkhā pamuccati.
english: restraint of body is good, restraint of speech is good, restraint of mind is good, restraint is everywhere good, a monastic who is restrained everywhere is liberated from all suffering.
notes: Note that restraint of body at this point forms a bridge between categories, on the one hand it is the last of the five-fold sense-spheres; and on the other it is the first of the three courses of action.

pali: Hatthasaṁyatŏ pādasaṁyato, vācāya saṁyatŏ saṁyatuttamo, ajjhattarato samāhito, eko santusito: tam-āhu bhikkhuṁ.
english: One who controls his hands, controls his feet, controls his speech, controls the (mind) supreme, with inner delight and composure, solitary, content: that one is called a monastic.
notes: The comm. explains it to mean one who personally delights in cultivating his meditation object.

pali: Yo mukhasaṁyato bhikkhu, mantabhāṇī anuddhato, atthaṁ Dhammañ-ca dīpeti, madhuraṁ tassa bhāsitaṁ.
english: That monastic who restrains the mouth, who speaks well, and who is modest, who explains the meaning of the Dhamma, his speech is sweet.

pali: Dhammārāmo Dhammarato, Dhammaṁ anuvicintayaṁ, Dhammaṁ anussaraṁ bhikkhu, Saddhammā na parihāyati.
english: The one who finds pleasure in the Dhamma, delights in Dhamma, reflects on Dhamma, the monastic who remembers Dhamma, does not abandon the Good Dhamma.

pali: Salābhaṁ nātimaññeyya, nāññesaṁ pihayaṁ care, aññesaṁ pihayaṁ bhikkhu samādhiṁ nādhigacchati.
english: One should not despise one’s own gains, one should not live envious of others, the monastic who is envious of others does not attain concentration.

pali: Appalābho pi ce bhikkhu salābhaṁ nātimaññati, taṁ ve devā pasaṁsanti suddhājīviṁ atanditaṁ.
english: Even if a monastic gains little he should not despise his gains, even the very gods praise the one of pure life who is diligent.

pali: Sabbaso nāmarūpasmiṁ yassa natthi mamāyitaṁ, asatā ca na socati, sa ve bhikkhū ti vuccati.
english: The one who does not have fondness at all for mind and body, and who grieves not for what does not exist, is surely called a monastic.

pali: Mettāvihārī yo bhikkhu, pasanno Buddhasāsane, adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: That monastic who dwells in loving-kindness, with faith in Buddha’s dispensation, should attain the state of peace, the joy in stilling of (all) conditions.

pali: Siñca bhikkhu imaṁ nāvaṁ, sittā te lahum-essati, chetvā rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca, tato Nibbānam-ehisi.
english: Please bail out this boat, monastic, when bailed out it will go lightly, cutting off passion and hatred, from here one will go to Nibbāna.

pali: Pañca chinde, pañca jahe, pañca cuttaribhāvaye, pañca saṅgātigo bhikkhu oghatiṇṇo ti vuccati.
english: One should cut off five, one should abandon five, one should cultivate five more, the monastic who surmounts five attachments is called a flood-crosser.
notes: The comm. explains it thus: one should cut off the five lower destinations, abandon the five lower fetters, cultivate five spiritual faculties; the five attachments are through passion, hatred, delusion, conceit and views.

pali: Jhāya, bhikkhu, mā ca pāmado, mā te kāmaguṇe bhamassu cittaṁ, mā lohaguḷaṁ gilī, pamatto, mā kandi: ‘Dukkham-idan’-ti ḍayhamāno.
english: Meditate, monastic, do not be heedless, do not let your mind swirl around in strands of desire, do not, heedless, swallow a (hot) iron ball, do not, while burning, cry: ‘This is suffering.’

pali: Natthi jhānaṁ apaññassa, paññā natthi ajhāyato, yamhi jhānañ-ca paññā ca sa ve Nibbānasantike.
english: There is no concentration for one without wisdom, there is no wisdom for one without concentration, the one who has both concentration and wisdom is indeed in the presence of Nibbāna.

pali: Suññāgāraṁ paviṭṭhassa, santacittassa bhikkhuno, amānusī ratī hoti sammā Dhammaṁ vipassato.
english: For the one who has entered an empty place, a monastic with a peaceful mind, there is superhuman delight from insight into true Dhamma.

pali: Yato yato sammasati khandhānaṁ udayabbayaṁ labhatī pītipāmojjaṁ, amataṁ taṁ vijānataṁ.
english: Whoever has right mindfulness regarding the rise and fall of the components (of mind and body) gains joy and happiness, that is the deathless state for the one who knows.

pali: Tatrāyam-ādi bhavati idha paññassa bhikkhuno: indriyagutti santuṭṭhī: pātimokkhe ca saṁvaro.
english: This is the very beginning for the wise monastic here: contentment, guarding the senses, and restraint in the regulations.

pali: Mitte bhajassu kalyāṇe suddhājīve atandite, paṭisanthāravuttassa ācārakusalo siyā, tato pāmojjabahulo, dukkhassantaṁ karissati.
english: One should resort to spiritual friends, ones of pure life, ones who are diligent, one should be of friendly disposition, one who will be skilful in his conduct, rejoicing frequently because of that, one will make an end to suffering.

pali: Vassikā viya pupphāni maddavāni pamuñcati, evaṁ rāgañ-ca dosañ-ca vippamuñcetha bhikkhavo.
english: Just as striped jasmine casts off its withered flowers, so, monastics, cast off (all) passion and hatred.

pali: Santakāyo santavāco, santavā susamāhito, vantalokāmiso bhikkhu upasanto ti vuccati.
english: Calm in body and calm in speech, having calmness and composure, having thrown off worldly gain the monastic is called one at peace.

pali: Attanā codayattānaṁ, paṭimāsettam-attanā, so attagutto satimā sukhaṁ bhikkhu vihāhisi.
english: By oneself one should censure self, by oneself one should be controlled, he who guards himself, mindful, will live happily, monastic.

pali: Attā hi attano nātho, attā hi attano gati, tasmā saṁyamayattānaṁ assaṁ bhadraṁ va vāṇijo.
english: Self is the protector of self, self is the refuge of self, therefore one should restrain oneself, as a merchant his noble horse.

pali: Pāmojjabahulo bhikkhu, pasanno Buddhasāsane, adhigacche padaṁ santaṁ, saṅkhārūpasamaṁ sukhaṁ.
english: The monastic, having much happiness, with faith in the dispensation of the Buddha, could attain to the state of peace, happy in the stilling of (all) conditions.

pali: Yo have daharo bhikkhu yuñjati Buddhasāsane, sŏ imaṁ lokaṁ pabhāseti, abbhā mutto va candimā.
english: That young monastic who is devoted to the Buddha’s dispensation, shines forth in this world, like the moon freed from a cloud.

pali: Chinda sotaṁ parakkamma, kāme panuda, brāhmaṇa, saṅkhārānaṁ khayaṁ ñatvā, akataññūsi, brāhmaṇa.
english: Strive and cut off the stream, remove desire, brahmin, knowing the destruction of the conditioned, be one who knows that which is not made, brahmin.
notes: What is not made is Nibbāna.

pali: Yadā dvayesu dhammesu pāragū hoti brāhmaṇo, athassa sabbe saṁyogā atthaṁ gacchanti jānato.
english: When a brahmin has, through two things, crossed over, then, for one who knows, all the fetters are laid to rest.
notes: I.e. calmness (samatha) and insight (vipassanā).

pali: Yassa pāraṁ apāraṁ vā pārāpāraṁ na vijjati, vītaddaraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: For whom the near shore, the far shore or both do not exist, free of anxiety, being detached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Jhāyiṁ virajam-āsīnaṁ, katakiccaṁ anāsavaṁ, uttamatthaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: The meditator sitting down, the one who is dustless, who has done his duty, without pollutants, who has reached the ultimate good, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Divā tapati ādicco, rattiṁābhāti candimā, sannaddho khattiyo tapati, jhāyī tapati brāhmaṇo, atha sabbam-ahorattiṁ Buddho tapati tejasā.
english: The sun is radiant by day, the moon shines by night, the accoutred noble is radiant, the meditating brahmin is radiant, yet every day and night the Buddha is radiant through his power.

pali: Bāhitapāpo ti brāhmaṇo, samacariyā samaṇo ti vuccati, pabbājayam-attano malaṁ tasmā pabbajito ti vuccati.
english: Warding off wickedness one is called a brahmin, one living austerely is said to be an ascetic, * because of driving forth (all) stain from oneself one is said to be one who has gone forth.

pali: Na brāhmaṇassa pahareyya, nāssa muñcetha brāhmaṇo, dhī brāhmaṇassa hantāraṁ, tato: dhī yassa muñcati.
english: A brahmin should not hit a brahmin, nor should he abandon him, woe to the one who strikes a brahmin, further: woe to the one who abandons him.

pali: Na brāhmaṇass’ etad-akiñci seyyo: yadā nisedho manaso piyehi, yato yato hiṁsamano nivattati, tato tato sammati-m-eva dukkhaṁ.
english: It is no little good for the brahmin: when the mind is held back from what is dear, whenever his mind turns back from violence, then there is a calming of suffering.

pali: Yassa kāyena vācāya manasā natthi dukkataṁ, saṁvutaṁ tīhi ṭhānehi, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: For whom there is no wrong-doing bodily, verbally or mentally, being restrained in (these) three things, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yamhā Dhammaṁ vijāneyya Sammāsambuddhadesitaṁ, sakkaccaṁ taṁ namasseyya, aggihuttaṁ va brāhmaṇo.
english: That one from whom one learned Dhamma taught by the Perfect Sambuddha, with respect bow down to him, like brahmin (bows) at fire-sacrifice.

pali: Na jaṭāhi na gottena, na jaccā hoti brāhmaṇo, yamhi saccañ-ca Dhammo ca, so sucī so va brāhmaṇo.
english: Not because of matted hair, family or birth is one a true brahmin, in whom there is truth and Dhamma, that one is pure, that one is surely a brahmin.

pali: Kiṁ te jaṭāhi dummedha, kiṁ te ajinasāṭiyā? Abbhantaraṁ te gahanaṁ, bāhiraṁ parimajjasi.
english: Why do you have your hair matted, stupid one, and why your deer-skin? Within you there is a jungle, you (only) polish the outside.
notes: Comm: a jungle of defilements.

pali: Paṁsukūladharaṁ jantuṁ, kisaṁ dhamanisanthataṁ, ekaṁ vanasmiṁ jhāyantaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: That one who wears discarded clothes, who is lean with protruding veins, who meditates alone in the forest, that one I say is a brahmin.
notes: Her name means the lean (Kisā) Gotamī.
This statement, which occurred also in vs. 385, 386 & 391 now becomes the refrain in all the remaining verses.

pali: Na cāhaṁ brāhmaṇaṁ brūmi yonijaṁ mattisambhavaṁ, bhovādī nāma so hoti sace hoti sakiñcano; akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: I do not call one a brahmin simply because of being born from a (certain) womb, that one is just one who says ‘bho’ if he is attached; having nothing and unattached, that one I say is a brahmin.
notes: From here to the end all the verses are drawn from Vāseṭṭhasutta (MN 98 and Sn 3.9); it is worth noting that this chapter is exceptionally long, and the parallel collections are much shorter.
It was a way for brahmins to address non-brahmins, implying their inferiority.

pali: Sabbasaṁyojanaṁ chetvā yo ve na paritassati, saṅgātigaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever has cut off all the fetters surely does not tremble, surmounting attachments, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Chetvā naddhiṁ varattañ-ca, sandānaṁ sahanukkamaṁ, ukkhittapalighaṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: (Whoever) has cut off the thong, the strap, the rope, together with the bridle, who has thrown off the obstacle and is awakened, that one I say is a brahmin.
notes: The commentary interprets the meaning as follows: Whoever has cut off hatred, craving, the sixty-two views together with the latent tendencies, and thrown off ignorance, that one I call a brahmin.

pali: Akkosaṁ vadhabandhañ-ca aduṭṭho yo titikkhati, khantībalaṁ balānīkaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever, being pure, forbears with punishment, bondage and abuse, having the strength of endurance, having an army of strengths,, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Akkodhanaṁ vatavantaṁ, sīlavantaṁ anussutaṁ, dantaṁ antimasārīraṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: (Whoever is) controlled of mind, dutiful, virtuous, taint-free, well-trained and in his last body, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Vāri pokkharapatte va, āragge-r-iva sāsapo, yo na lippati kāmesu, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Like water on the lotus leaf, like a mustard seed on a needle, he who is unsmeared by desires, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yo dukkhassa pajānāti idheva khayam-attano, pannabhāraṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever knows right here the destruction of his suffering, putting down the burden, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Gambhīrapaññaṁ medhāviṁ, maggāmaggassa kovidaṁ, uttamatthaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: The deeply wise sagacious one, skilled in what is path and not path, who has reached the ultimate good, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Asaṁsaṭṭhaṁ gahaṭṭhehi anāgārehi cūbhayaṁ, anokasāriṁ appicchaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: (Whoever) doesn’t mix with either householders or the houseless, wandering homeless, with few desires, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Nidhāya daṇḍaṁ bhūtesu tasesu thāvaresu ca, yo na hanti na ghāteti, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: * Whoever has laid down the stick (used) against fearful and fearless beings, who neither hurts nor kills, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Aviruddhaṁ viruddhesu, attadaṇḍesu nibbutaṁ, sādānesu anādānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Being friendly with the hostile, calm amongst those holding a stick, not attached amongst those attached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yassa rāgo ca doso ca māno makkho ca pātito, sāsapo-r-iva āraggā, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever has dropped off passion and hatred, conceit and anger, like a mustard seed from a needle, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Akakkasaṁ viññapaniṁ giraṁ saccaṁ udīraye, yāya nābhisaje kañci, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: (Whoever) speaks a word of truth that is informed and is not coarse, through which no one would be angry, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yodha dīghaṁ va rassaṁ vā aṇuṁ-thūlaṁ subhāsubhaṁ, loke adinnaṁ nādiyati, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: * Whoever in the world does not take what is not given, long, short, small, large, attractive or unattractive, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Āsā yassa na vijjanti asmiṁ loke paramhi ca, nirāsayaṁ visaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: For the one who has no longings in this world or in the next world, being without longings, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yassālayā na vijjanti, aññāya akathaṅkathī, amatogadhaṁ anuppattaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: For the one who has no desires, who, through knowledge, is without doubt, who has reached immersion in the deathless, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yodha puññañ-ca pāpañ-ca ubho saṅgaṁ upaccagā, asokaṁ virajaṁ suddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever here has overcome clinging to both merit and demerit, who is griefless, dustless and pure, that one I say is a brahmin.
notes: In the Majjhima commentary to Vāseṭṭhasuttaṁ pāpaṁ here is defined as apuññaṁ, which I follow in the translation.

pali: Candaṁ va vimalaṁ suddhaṁ, vippasannam-anāvilaṁ, nandībhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: (Whoever) just like the moon is stainless, pure, clear and undisturbed, has destroyed joy in existence, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yo imaṁ palipathaṁ duggaṁ saṁsāraṁ moham-accagā, tiṇṇo pāragato jhāyī, anejo akathaṅkathī, anupādāya nibbuto, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: He who has crossed the difficult and dangerous path through births and deaths and delusion, the meditator who has crossed over to the further shore, free of lust and free of doubt, unattached and cooled down, that one I say is a brahmin.
notes: The commentary says: Whoever has overcome the difficult path of passions and so forth, the inaccessible defilements, the round of births and deaths, the delusion of not having penetrated the four noble truths.

pali: Yodha kāme pahatvāna anāgāro paribbaje, kāmabhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever, giving up sensual desires, would wander homeless here, destroying desires and existence, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yodha taṇhaṁ pahatvāna, anāgāro paribbaje, taṇhābhavaparikkhīṇaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever, giving up craving, would wander homeless here, destroying craving and existence, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Hitvā mānusakaṁ yogaṁ, dibbaṁ yogaṁ upaccagā, sabbayogavisaṁyuttaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Abandoning the human yoke, overcoming the divine yoke, being unattached to all yokes, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Hitvā ratiñ-ca aratiñ-ca, sītibhūtaṁ nirūpadhiṁ, sabbalokābhibhuṁ vīraṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Abandoning delight and aversion, cooled off and free from cleaving, a hero who vanquished the whole world, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Cutiṁ yo vedi sattānaṁ upapattiñ-ca sabbaso, asattaṁ sugataṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever knows in every way beings’ passing and their rebirth, unattached, fortunate, awake, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yassa gatiṁ na jānanti devā gandhabbamānusā – khīṇāsavaṁ Arahantaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: For the one whose destiny is unknown to gods, gandhabbas and men – being pollutant-free, an Arahat, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Yassa pure ca pacchā ca majjhe ca natthi kiñcanaṁ, akiñcanaṁ anādānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: For whom there is nothing in the past, the future or the present, having nothing and unattached, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Usabhaṁ pavaraṁ vīraṁ, mahesiṁ vijitāvinaṁ, anejaṁ nhātakaṁ buddhaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: A noble leader, heroic, a great seer, victorious, free of lust, cleansed and awakened, that one I say is a brahmin.

pali: Pubbenivāsaṁ yo vedī, saggāpāyañ-ca passati, atho jātikkhayaṁ patto, abhiññāvosito muni, sabbavositavosānaṁ, tam-ahaṁ brūmi brāhmaṇaṁ.
english: Whoever knows their former lives, and sees heaven and the downfall, and has attained birth’s destruction, the sage, accomplished in deep knowledge, who is accomplished in all accomplishments, that one I say is a brahmin.
